CHAIRMAN’S MESSAGE
ADITYA BIRLA FASHION AND RETAIL LIMITED INTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT FY 2025-26In a global landscape defined by volatility, geopolitical 
tension, and accelerating technological change, FY26 has been a milestone year for the Group. Our large manufacturing businesses have consolidated their leadership positions, our newer ventures are scaling with conviction, and our legacy consumer businesses are being reshaped for a new era of growth. Across this diverse portfolio, one force continues to anchor our progress— trust.
Trust is often viewed as an intangible asset. In reality, 
it is one of the most consequential forms of capital an institution can possess. In periods of uncertainty, markets can turn volatile and competitive advantages can erode. Trust, however, compounds. It enables organisations to make long-term investments when others hesitate, to navigate disruption with credibility, and to emerge stronger from periods of change.
For a group such as ours, trust extends far beyond the 
relationship between a company and its customers. It is reflected in the confidence of shareholders who support long-term value creation, the commitment of employees who choose to build their careers with us, the faith of partners and suppliers who invest alongside us, and the confidence of communities and governments that see us as a responsible participant in economic progress. Each of these constituencies grants an institution something invaluable: the licence to grow.
This is particularly relevant at a time when businesses 
are being asked to do more than deliver financial performance. They are expected to navigate technological disruption, manage increasingly complex supply chains, create meaningful employment, steward natural resources responsibly and contribute to social progress. Meeting these expectations requires more than scale or strategy. It requires credibility built over years and, in many cases, decades.
The strength of our portfolio today reflects the cumulative 
effect of that credibility. It has allowed us to invest through cycles, pursue transformation with confidence and attract talent, capital, and partnerships that strengthen our competitive position. 
Global Economy in 2025
The global economy maintained its trajectory through 2025 despite elevated tariffs, policy uncertainty, and geopolitical tensions. The impact of tariff measures was less severe than projections had suggested, and growth across major economies remained broadly stable.
World trade expanded faster than anticipated in 2025, 
as demand for AI-driven capex offset the effects of trade policy uncertainty and higher tariffs. The volume of world merchandise trade grew by 4.6%, compared to a forecast of 2.4%. For the second consecutive year, Asian economies were the largest contributors to total world trade volume growth, accounting for 3.2 percentage points of the 4.6% total — or 71% of the overall increase.
Trade in 2025 was also supported by investment in 
AI infrastructure, demand in emerging markets, fiscal and monetary expansion in advanced economies, and CREATING VALUE FOR ALL
KUMAR MANGALAM BIRLA
CHAIRMAN OF THE ADITYA BIRLA GROUP

India in FY2025–26: Domestic Demand Carries the 
Economy Forward
Against a challenging global backdrop marked by US tariff 
escalations and mounting trade policy uncertainty, the Indian economy demonstrated remarkable resilience during FY26. Real GDP growth accelerated to 7.6 percent, up from 7.1 percent in FY25, cementing India’s position as the fastest-growing major economy globally. 
This performance was underpinned by robust domestic 
demand, low inflation, and a broad pro-growth reform agenda. On the demand side, private consumption grew 7.7% year-on-year, supported by income tax reductions and rationalisation of GST rates. 
Economic activity was broad-based. On the supply side, 
manufacturing gained momentum, driven by the automobile and fast-moving consumer goods sectors. The services sector benefited from demand in retail trade, hospitality, transportation, and real estate. India also made progress in containing inflation, with the headline rate averaging 2% in FY26, down from 4.7% the previous year. 
India’s economic prospects for FY27 carry both 
opportunities and risks. Growth is projected at 6.6% by RBI, marginally revised down due to the effects of the Middle East conflict, which has pushed up global energy prices and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. India nonetheless remains among the fastest-growing major economies globally.
Private consumption is expected to remain the primary 
driver of growth, though elevated global oil prices are likely to feed into domestic inflationary pressures. The GST rate reductions introduced in September 2025 are expected to partially offset this impact. Investment is projected to continue, supported by government capital expenditure, improved trade access through recently concluded free trade agreements, and a stable financial sector. 
India’s macroeconomic position, including foreign 
exchange reserves, a narrowing current account, and a path of fiscal consolidation, provides some buffer against external shocks. The pace of the renewable energy transition, the credibility of fiscal policy, and the implementation of newly concluded trade agreements will be factors that determine the trajectory of growth in the coming years.
Aditya Birla Group: In our people we trust
At the Aditya Birla Group, trust is built through experience. It is earned in thousands of everyday interactions—when people are given opportunities to learn, when careers progress on merit, when leaders are accessible, when commitments are honoured, and when employees know they can depend on the organisation through moments that matter.
Over time, these experiences shape how people feel 
about the Group. They influence whether talented individuals choose to join us, whether they see a future with us, and whether they are willing to invest their energy and ambition here over the long term.
The progress we have made across talent, leadership, 
culture and employee experience during the year reflects this enduring focus.
Trust in Competence: Helping people succeed from 
day one
The employee experience begins long before an individual 
settles into a role. The quality of hiring, onboarding and early support often shapes how quickly people become effective and how confidently they navigate a new environment.
During the year, we onboarded more than 11,700 
employees, including over 80 senior leaders, across businesses and functions. Structured hiring and onboarding processes, clear communication and timely feedback helped create a stronger experience for candidates and new joiners alike.We also continued to simplify the day-to-day employee 
experience through technology. Mobile-first onboarding and AI-enabled platforms such as AVA, which recorded more than 700,000 interactions during the year, improved accessibility, and delivered greater consistency at scale.
Capability building remains central to long-term success. 
Employees are more likely to perform with confidence when they have access to the skills, knowledge and support required to succeed. Through Gyanodaya, our Global Centre for Leadership Training, and other business-led initiatives, we delivered more than 280 programmes, reaching over 8,500 employees across technical, functional, behavioural and leadership domains. Ninety-eight per cent of employees accessed digital or blended learning through the Gyanodaya Virtual Campus (GVC). In addition, an intense 3-month group-wide learning initiative, the ‘Learning Fest’, engaged more than 39,000 employees, a fourfold increase over the previous year.
Managers play a critical role in shaping this experience. 
Through coaching, feedback and day-to-day guidance, they influence how employees learn, grow and navigate their careers. We therefore continue to invest in strengthening leadership capability across the Group.
Trust in Growth: Building careers across the Group
The strength of an organisation is often reflected in the opportunities it creates for its people. During the year, more than 6,400 employees moved across roles, functions, businesses or geographies. This is, by all accounts, a very significant number. These movements reflect the scale and diversity of opportunities available across the Group and reinforce our promise of A World of Opportunities.
Internal mobility also provides an important measure of organisational confidence. Of the 6,400+ movements during the year, more than 470 were across businesses. At senior leadership levels, cross-business mobility accounted for 15% of movements, strengthening leadership depth across the portfolio. Nearly 69% of senior management roles were filled through internal hiring, reflecting the quality and readiness of leadership talent developed within the Group.
These outcomes are supported by a disciplined approach 
to identifying and developing talent. 27% of employees form part of the Group Talent Pool. We have also built a strong pipeline of future leaders.
Our ability to attract high-quality talent continues to 
reflect the strength of our employer brand. Diversity hiring stood at 19% during the year, while retail businesses achieved 40% women hiring. Women’s representation within the leadership cadre increased by 8%. Seventy-four per cent of new hires were below the age of 35, with Gen Z accounting for 39% of all new joiners. 
The Group also received recognition across leading 
platforms including LinkedIn, the Top Employers Institute, Forbes and the Financial Times. 
Trust in Care: Supporting people and families
The employee experience extends beyond the workplace. Health, wellbeing and support systems influence how people feel, perform and engage over the long term.
Through our health, wellbeing and insurance initiatives, 
we supported employees and their families in meaningful ways. During the year, more than 8,600 counselling sessions were availed by employees, while workmen and staff accessed a further 3,100+ sessions, reflecting growing awareness and acceptance of mental wellbeing support. In parallel, over 3,400 eligible employees underwent annual health check-ups, reinforcing our focus on preventive care.
These efforts are translating into measurable outcomes. 
Among Mumbai-based employees, the proportion of individuals in the high-risk category, in terms of health, declined from 21% to 10%, while the low-risk category increased from 48% to 56%.
Employee sentiment continues to reflect this strong 
foundation. In our Annual employee survey, Vibes 2026, 96% of employees expressed pride in being part of the Group, 90% said they would recommend us as a great place to work, and 93% reported that their business inspires them to do their best work every day.Against a challenging global backdrop marked

Your Company’s Performance
FY26 marked an important step in your Company’s transformation journey. Despite a challenging external environment, the year was characterised by meaningful strategic progress across the business. Investments made over the past few years in brand building, product innovation, customer experience, digital capabilities and new growth platforms are beginning to translate into stronger business performance and a clearer path towards sustainable, profitable growth.
Over the years, your Company has built a distinctive 
fashion and lifestyle ecosystem comprising India’s largest ethnic wear platform, a leading luxury retail business, a dominant masstige and value retail play, and one of the country’s largest digital-first fashion portfolio. This diversified presence enables us to serve consumers across multiple occasions, lifestyles, price points and channels, while positioning the Company to participate meaningfully in India’s evolving consumer story.
FY26 marked an important transition from building these 
growth platforms to scaling them with greater focus and discipline. Across the business, our priorities were centred on strengthening execution, enhancing fashion relevance, expanding omni-channel capabilities, elevating retail experiences and building stronger operating capabilities. These initiatives are driving sustainable growth while laying the foundation for long-term value creation.
The progress achieved during the year reinforces our 
confidence in the strategy adopted and the opportunities that lie ahead. Supported by a balanced mix of scaled businesses and emerging growth engines, strong brands and a consumer-centric approach, we believe your Company is well positioned to create sustainable value for its stakeholders.
India’s Fashion Market Is Poised for Sustained Long-
Term Growth 
India’s fashion and lifestyle industry continues to offer a 
compelling long-term growth opportunity. Rising incomes, favorable demographics, urbanization and increasing fashion consciousness are reshaping consumer behavior, with apparel becoming an expression of identity, aspiration and lifestyle. Consumers today are seeking greater choice, better quality and more seamless access across physical and digital channels.
Industry estimates suggest that India’s apparel retail 
market could be more than ₹ 14 lakh crore by FY30, with 
organized retail growing faster than the overall market. The shift towards branded apparel, premiumization, omni-channel retail and digital commerce creates a favorable environment for companies with trusted brands, strong execution capabilities and differentiated proposition to build a compelling play.
While the near-term operating environment may continue 
to be shaped by geopolitical developments, inflationary pressures and fluctuations in consumer sentiment, India’s long-term consumption fundamentals remain strong. With its strong portfolio of brands, growing omni-channel ecosystem and focus on consumer-led innovation, Your Company is well positioned to fully leverage this opportunity.
FY26 Performance: Strengthening Momentum, 
Creating Value
FY26 saw your Company’s strategic priorities translate into 
encouraging business outcomes. Revenue grew by 11% year-on-year to ₹ 8,177 crore, supported by broad-based growth 
across the portfolio, stronger retail execution and continued progress in omni-channel capabilities. 
Alongside revenue growth, the Company continued to 
strengthen earnings quality through disciplined execution, while investing in technology, retail expansion and future growth platforms. These investments are strengthening the Company’s long-term competitive position while creating a stronger foundation for sustainable and profitable growth.
Digital initiatives remain a key growth driver, with 
e-commerce revenue increasing by over 20% during the year and contributing approximately 16% of total revenue. At the same time, the Company expanded its physical footprint by adding over 180 stores and nearly 0.6 million square feet of net retail space, further enhancing accessibility across priority markets.
Today, your Company reaches consumers through one 
of India’s largest fashion retail networks, comprising 1,273 stores spanning over 7.9 million square feet, complemented by a strong presence across brand websites and leading digital marketplaces. This integrated omni-channel ecosystem enables us to serve consumers seamlessly across touchpoints, strengthening engagement while creating a scalable platform for long-term growth.
Strengthening Leadership Across Key Business 
Segments
Masstige and Value Retail SegmentIndia’s expanding middle class, rising disposable incomes 
and increasing preference for organised retail continue to create a compelling long-term opportunity in the masstige and value fashion segment. Consumers today are increasingly seeking contemporary fashion, superior quality, differentiated shopping experiences, and omnichannel access. These structural shifts provide a strong foundation for sustained growth and reinforce the strategic importance of this business within your Company’s portfolio.
During the year, Pantaloons continued to make 
meaningful progress in its strategic transformation, with a clear focus on strengthening its fashion authority and enhancing the overall consumer proposition. The business accelerated its efforts towards fashion freshness, premiumisation, improved merchandising and elevated in-store experiences, while further strengthening its omni-channel capabilities. Brand-building initiatives, including the appointment of its first celebrity brand ambassador and digitally led consumer campaigns, helped deepen consumer engagement and strengthen the brand’s contemporary appeal. Together, these initiatives are positioning Pantaloons as a sharper, more relevant and increasingly differentiated fashion destination for the modern Indian consumer.
Our value fashion retail format, OWND, also continued 
to strengthen its presence during the year, expanding its footprint with the addition of 34 stores. While expansion remained an important priority, equal emphasis was placed on optimizing the operating model, elevating merchandise architecture and building a scalable platform for long-term growth. As the business continues to evolve, we believe OWND is well positioned to address the growing demand for affordable fashion, and become an important contributor to the Company’s future growth journey.
Ethnic Wear Segment
Ethnic wear continues to be one of the most attractive growth opportunities within India’s fashion industry, supported by increasing premiumisation, rising aspirations and sustained demand across wedding, festive and everyday occasions. Your Company has built India’s largest and most comprehensive ethnic wear platform, addressing the full spectrum of consumer needs—from luxury couture and designer fashion, to premium occasion wear and branded ethnic apparel.

Our Premium Ethnic Brands, comprising TASVA, Jaypore

Luxury Retail Segment
India’s luxury retail market is at an inflection point, driven by rising affluence, increasing global exposure, evolving consumer aspirations and growing demand for premium experiences. Luxury consumption is expanding beyond traditional metropolitan markets, creating a significant long-term opportunity for organised players with strong brand partnerships, differentiated retail formats and deep consumer understanding.
Your Company has built a robust luxury portfolio 
comprising The Collective, Mono Brands and Galeries Lafayette, positioning it across multiple segments of the super-premium and luxury market. The Collective and Mono Brands continued to strengthen their leadership through a curated portfolio of global brands, an increasingly loyal customer base, expanding omni-channel capabilities and selective retail expansion. 
A defining milestone during the year was the launch of 
Galeries Lafayette in Mumbai, introducing one of the world’s most iconic luxury department store in India. More than a retail destination, Galeries Lafayette represents a first-of-its-kind, experiential luxury concept, bringing together global luxury brands, curated experiences and immersive consumer engagement under a single roof. Together with The Collective, it significantly strengthens your Company’s luxury ecosystem and positions ABFRL to participate meaningfully in the next phase of India’s premiumisation journey.
Digital -First Brands
TMRW continues to strengthen its position as your Company’s digital-first growth platform, built to serve the evolving aspirations of India’s next generation of consumers. As fashion discovery increasingly shifts towards digital ecosystems, social influence and creator-led engagement, this platform is well positioned to build contemporary brands that are relevant, agile and capable of scaling across multiple consumer segments.
During the year, TMRW continued to strengthen its 
portfolio through product innovation, premiumisation and richer consumer engagement. The focus remained on building stronger brands, improving the quality of growth and creating a more sustainable business model, while leveraging technology and data to enhance consumer experiences and deepen customer relationships.
As the platform matures, TMRW is progressively evolving 
from a digital-first business model into an omni-channel platform led by expansion of exclusive brand stores alongside its strong online presence. We believe this integrated approach will enable TMRW to build enduring consumer brands.
CONCLUSION
In a world characterised by constant change, trust, becomes an even more valuable source of resilience 
and differentiation. In my view, trust is the currency that matters. 
Over the years, one of the most encouraging aspects of the Aditya Birla Group’s journey has been 
the way trust in the Group has translated across businesses, strengthening consumer affinity, deepening stakeholder relationships and reinforcing the resilience of our portfolio. 
Trust, after all, provides a strong foundation for growth. It gives us the confidence to pursue trans-
formation within our existing businesses and the conviction to build new growth platforms for the fu-ture. More importantly, it allows us to do so with the support of those who matter most to our success—our customers, employees, partners, investors, and communities.
— Kumar Mangalam Birla
Chairman, Aditya Birla GroupAccelerating Our Sustainability Journey  
As we build the next phase of ABFRL, sustainability will 
continue to be a source of long-term competitive advantage rather than a parallel business agenda. Fashion is undergoing a fundamental shift, with consumers, investors and other stakeholders increasingly expecting businesses to combine growth with responsibility. At ABFRL, we see this transition as an opportunity to build stronger brands, more resilient value chains and a future-ready organisation that is better equipped to create enduring value.
Over the years, we have built a strong foundation, and 
our focus now is on embedding sustainability deeper into the way we design products, source responsibly, operate our businesses and engage with our stakeholders. As we move forward, we will continue to strengthen our climate commitments, advance circularity, improve supply-chain accountability and leverage technology to enhance transparency and decision-making. Our objective remains clear—to create long-term value for shareholders while contributing positively to society and leaving a lighter footprint on the environment.
Poised for the Next Phase of Growth 
We remain committed to shaping a future-ready fashion and lifestyle company at the forefront of India’s evolving retail landscape. The opportunity ahead is significant, and it demands sharper execution and greater agility. We are focused on proactively adapting to evolving consumer preferences, strengthening fashion freshness, deepening omni-channel engagement and delivering superior retail experiences. We will continue to invest in our brands while ensuring that growth is pursued with discipline, capital efficiency and a clear path towards stronger profitability and cash generation.
Guided by a clear vision, powered by our talented 
teams and anchored in operational excellence, we remain committed to creating enduring value for our shareholders, customers, employees, partners and communities.

Our ethnic portfolio continued to expand its reach, with 
over 680 stores across key markets, including over 80 new store additions during the year. This growing footprint gives us the ability to serve consumers across a wide spectrum of occasions, from weddings and festivities to contemporary ethnic and everyday wear.
The Designer-Led Brands portfolio, comprising Sab -
yasachi, Shantnu & Nikhil, Tarun Tahiliani, and House of Masaba, continued to drive strong results. These brands remain important anchors of our bridge-to-luxury and luxury ethnic strategy, supported by their distinctive de -
sign identities, strong brand equity and deep connection with Indian craft and culture. During the year, growth was supported by category extensions, craft-led and contempo -
rary launches, and deeper brand collaborations across the portfolio. The business continued to deliver robust growth along with strong double-digit profitability.
The Premium Ethnic Brands portfolio, including TASVA, 
Jaypore, and TCNS brands, also made encouraging prog-ress during the year. TASVA maintained its growth momen -
tum, delivering consistent double-digit like-to-like growth for both the quarter and the full year. The brand continues to build strength across product, retail experience, and brand image, with a clear focus on scaling across India’s key wedding markets. Its network now stands at 94 stores, and we will continue to expand selectively in high-potential locations.
Jaypore achieved strong double-digit growth, under -
pinned by strategic store expansion and healthy momen -
tum across its e-commerce channels. With a network of 44 stores, the brand continues to strengthen its position in the premium artisanal and craft-led ethnic wear space, offering a differentiated proposition to consumers seeking authen -
ticity, design, and craftsmanship.
TCNS made meaningful progress on both growth and 
profitability. The business delivered 10% like-to-like growth, driven by a sharper product proposition, refreshed col -
lections and new launches that resonated well with con -
sumers. Full-year cash losses reduced by more than half compared to last year, reflecting focused execution and tighter operating discipline. The launch of the first W for Woman flagship store in Mumbai was an important mile -
stone, bringing the refreshed brand proposition to life in a stronger retail format.
Together, our Designer-Led and Premium Ethnic busi -
nesses give your Company a strong and differentiated pres -
ence in one of India’s most attractive fashion categories. As we move ahead, our focus will be on scaling these brands with improving store productivity, strengthening profitabil -
ity and building a comprehensive ethnic wear platform that serves consumers across segments, occasions, and price points.
Luxury Segment
The Luxury business continued to build momentum during FY26, supported by a portfolio that brings together The Collective, Fred Perry, Polo Ralph Lauren, Ted Baker London, Hackett (Mono Brands) and Galeries Lafayette. Together, these formats allow your Company to address distinct parts of the super-premium and luxury market, from curated multi-brand retail to exclusive brand-led ex -
periences and large-format luxury destinations.
During the year, The Collective and Mono Brands de -
livered revenue growth of around 9% on a profitable basis, supported by positive like-to-like growth. The performance was driven by the strength of the international brand portfolio, strong customer relationships and a differentiated retail experience. The business also expanded its footprint with the addition of 8 new stores, while continuing to scale in a measured manner through selective market expansion, improved omni-channel capabilities and deeper engage -

The launch of Galeries Lafayette in Mumbai was an 
important milestone in our luxury journey. It brings to India a globally recognised luxury department store format and creates a distinctive destination for premium consumers. With its curated brand mix, elevated store environment, and experiential approach, the format is designed to offer much more than conventional retail.
Galeries Lafayette is still in its early phase and our

Alongside The Collective and Mono Brands, it adds depth and scale to our luxury play and strengthens our ability to participate in India’s growing premium consumption opportunity.

TMRW continued to make strong progress with its focus around creating new-age fashion and lifestyle brands for a generation of consumers whose discovery, engagement and purchase journeys are increasingly shaped by digital platforms, social communities and creator-led influence.
During FY26, the portfolio delivered robust revenue 
growth of 34%, while losses began to reduce through the year, reflecting a planned, gradual shift towards bet -
ter-quality and more sustainable growth. This progress was supported by sharper brand positioning, improved prod-uct-market fit, premiumisation initiatives and more focused consumer engagement across the portfolio.
Technology and data remained central to the way 
TMRW builds and scales its brands. These capabilities are helping the platform understand consumer preferences better, improve assortment decisions, enhance customer experience, and create stronger repeat engagement.
During the year, TMRW also expanded its offline pres -
ence in a calibrated manner, adding over 60 stores and taking the total network to 120 stores across brands. This selective expansion of exclusive brand stores, alongside its strong digital presence, is helping the platform build deep -
er consumer connect and improve brand visibility.
As TMRW scales, our priority will remain on strength -
ening brand fundamentals, improving unit economics, reducing losses, and building a portfolio of contemporary brands with the potential to become meaningful long-term businesses.
The Digital LeapWe continued to strengthen our digital and e-commerce 
capabilities across brands, with a clear focus on creating seamless, consistent and engaging consumer experienc -
es across touchpoints. Built on our proprietary in-house e-commerce platform, our digital ecosystem now includes dedicated brand websites, mobile applications and virtual stores, enabling our brands to engage consumers more effectively across both online and omni-channel journeys.
During the year, we made meaningful progress in mod -
ernizing our core technology infrastructure, strengthening data capabilities and embedding AI-led solutions across key areas of the business. AI-driven insights, customer an -
alytics, and data-led decision-making are helping us better understand consumer behavior, improve personalization, sharpen engagement and enhance operational efficiency.
These initiatives are enabling us to deliver more relevant 
and intuitive experiences to consumers, while building a digital foundation that is more agile, scalable, and fu -
ture-ready.
E-commerce continued to gain scale as an important 
growth channel, contributing around 16% of revenue during the year. With e-commerce revenue growing over 20% year-on-year, the channel reflects the increasing strength of our digital ecosystem and its ability to support deeper consumer engagement across online and omni-channel platforms.
Commitment to ReEarth Sustainability 3.0 Program ABFRL continues to advance its sustainability agenda 
through the ReEarth Sustainability Program, which re -
mains central to how we think about responsible growth and long-term value creation. Our efforts are focused on building a more future-ready business by driving progress across material innovation, circularity, traceability, resource efficiency, and responsible sourcing.
We are now moving into the next phase of our sustain -
ability journey — ReEarth Sustainability 3.0: Transforma -
tion. Beginning FY26, this phase represents a shift towards deeper, enterprise-wide action. Our ambition is to build comprehensive readiness for decarbonisation, scale circular practices, strengthen transparency across the value chain and support inclusive growth. This marks an evolution from embedding sustainability into business processes to creat -
ing broader, systemic impact.
Our sustainability efforts are also strengthened through 
collaborations with global partners, enabling us to explore new materials, improve supply-chain visibility, and acceler -
ate circular business models. These initiatives are helping us build greater resilience while responding to the expec -
tations of consumers, communities, investors and other stakeholders.
Alongside our environmental and governance priorities, 
we remain committed to creating meaningful social impact through our Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives. Our CSR programmes are designed to support inclusive devel -
opment and address priority community needs through measurable and outcome-oriented interventions.
During the year, the Company implemented CSR initia -
tives across Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Odisha, Delhi NCR, Meghalaya, and Andhra Pradesh, with a focus on education and skill development. Through these efforts, we aim to empower communities, enhance livelihood op -
portunities, and contribute to more inclusive and sustain -
able progress.
Charting the Future of Growth As we move into the next phase of our journey, our prior -
ities are firmly aligned towards building a stronger, more 
resilient, and future-ready fashion and lifestyle business. FY26 demonstrated that the investments made over the past few years in brands, distribution, digital capabilities and operating infrastructure are beginning to translate into tangible business outcomes.
During the year, your Company delivered healthy 
revenue growth along with improved margins, supported by scale benefits, sharper execution and better operating discipline across businesses. This progress reinforces our confidence in the strength of our portfolio and the long-term potential of the markets we serve.
While the consumption environment showed signs 
of improvement in the latter part of the year, we remain watchful of near-term volatility. However, the structural opportunity in organised fashion and lifestyle retail in India remains significant, supported by evolving consumer as -
pirations, premiumisation, increasing brand consciousness and the continued shift towards modern retail formats.
Our focus remains on scaling the businesses thought -
fully, improving profitability, strengthening customer engagement across channels and delivering differentiated retail experiences. We will continue to balance growth with financial discipline, ensuring that expansion is supported by stronger unit economics, operating leverage and sustain -
able cash generation.

LAUREN POLO For more than 50 years, Ralph Lauren has sought to inspire the dream of a better life through authenticity and timeless style. / / / FRED PERRY Triple Wimbledon champion Fred Perry played and fought his way through, always with style and despite the establishment. In 1952, he founded the Fred Perry brand, designing his first pique shirt. That shirt, would transcend sportswear to streetwear on the backs of generation after generation of British youth subcultures. It is the start and end of everything Fred does, because it’s more than a shirt – it’s a rite of passage, it’s the uniform of the non-uniform. Fred is proud to have a community of customers from all over the world, adopting the Fred Perry Shirt in their own unique way. Over the past 70 years, the Laurel Wreath has become a signature of both individuality and of belonging – from elite sports players, to fringe subcultures. The brand continues to celebrate diversity, with exciting collaborations with inspiring designers, musicians and artists.

ADITYA BIRLA FASHION RETAIL LIMITEDINTEGRATED ANNUAL REPORT FY 2025-263
We are pleased to share Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail 
Limited’s. (ABFRL’s) Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26. This comprehensive report provides the ability to create value, utilising both financial and non-financial resources.
This is our third integrated annual report which provides 
an overview of our performance, business strategy, operating environment, material issues, key risks and opportunities, governance, and approach to long-term sustainability.
This report covers operations of ABFRL, following the 
demerger of the Madura Fashion and Lifestyle business into a separate entity, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL).
Through our integrated report, we aim to provide stake-
holders with a deeper understanding of our value generation initiatives and our business approach in addressing key risks and opportunities.Restatement of Information There is no restatement of information due to demerger of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited and Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited.
Reporting Principles
Our Report is aligned with the International Integrated Reporting (<IR>) Framework of the Integrated Reporting and Connectivity Council (IRCC). The Report highlights how value is created over time by presenting our performance across the six capitals– financial, manufactured, human, intellectual, natural, and social and relationship.
The non-financial performance indicators disclosed are 
in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) 2021 Universal Standards and the Sustainability Account-ing Standards Board (SASB). In addition, the Report also complies with the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) as mandated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), and the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. Our reporting approach is further guided by the principles of the United Nations Global Compact (UNGC) and reflects our contribution to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs).
The preparation and presentation of non financial perfor-
mance disclosures in this report are aligned with the eight GRI 2021 reporting principles: Accuracy, Balance, Clarity, Comparability, Completeness, Sustainability Context, Timeli-ness, and Verifiability. These principles reinforce transparent, consistent, and reliable communication of our economic, environmental, and social performance while ensuring com-pliance with the applicable ‘in accordance’ requirements. 
The financial statements are prepared in compliance 
with the Indian Accounting Standards as prescribed under section 133 of the Companies Act 2013. These statements also comply with the relevant provisions of the Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) Rules, 2015, including sub-sequent amendments; the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, along with applicable SEBI circulars; the Secretarial Standards issued by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India; and other accounting principles general-ly accepted in India.
Reporting Period 
This report presents a consolidated and detailed account of our performance for the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026. We publish the report on an annual basis. The previous report was published in August 2025. The disclosures in-cluded herein reflect development, performance trends, and strategic focus areas relevant to the reporting year.
Reporting Boundary and Scope 
The report discloses our financial performance for the consolidated business, covering subsidiary business entities listed in the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report Section. The non-financial reporting boundary covers the TCNS business, Pantaloons, OWND and subsidiaries including Sabyasachi, Tasva, Shantnu & Nikhil (S&N), House of Masaba, and Jaypore. The reporting boundary includes Indian opera-tions as mentioned below.

Built on decades of consumer trust, we are shaping purpose-led fashion and life-
style brands that celebrate self-expression, elevate everyday wear and occasion wear, support responsible choices, and create distinctive retail experiences across India’s evolving fashion landscape.
Trust has been the cornerstone of Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited’s 
(ABFRL’s) journey, shaping enduring relationships with consumers, partners, employees and communities. As we enter a new phase of growth following the demerger, we are evolving into a sharper, more focused fashion and lifestyle company, positioned to serve the diverse Indian fashion market. With a portfolio spanning large-format retail, designer-led ethnic wear, luxury labels, contemporary fashion and new-age digital brands, we continue to create innovative fashion solu-tions that reflect changing lifestyles, cultural moments, aspirations and individual identities.
“Built on Trust. Building Brands with Purpose.” reflects our belief that endur-
ing fashion brands are built not only through scale, reach and market presence, but through meaningful relevance in consumers’ lives. Each brand in our port-folio is guided by a distinct purpose: to inspire self-expression, celebrate Indian craftsmanship, reimagine occasion dressing, deliver accessible style, elevate premium and luxury experiences, and make fashion more responsive to evolving consumer choices. From Pantaloons’ role in democratising fashion retail, Jaypore’s celebration of artisanal heritage, Tasva’s modern interpretation of ethnic mens-wear, and Sabyasachi’s luxury craftsmanship, to our digital-first brands designed for trend-conscious consumers, we are building deeper connections across every touchpoint.
Our purpose-led approach is strengthened by continuous investments in de-
sign capabilities, merchandise innovation, omnichannel retail, digital engagement, customer analytics and responsible business practices. As fashion cycles become faster and consumers seek more personalised, conscious and seamless experienc-es, we are embedding agility, creativity and sustainability into the way we design, source, retail and engage. This enables our brands to remain relevant across occa-sions, regions, channels and price points while supporting long-term value creation through stronger governance, operational discipline and consumer trust.
As we look ahead, trust remains our strongest fabric - and purpose our guiding 
thread. Building on a legacy of excellence and powered by a portfolio of distinctive brands, we are shaping the future of fashion and lifestyle retail in India by creating products, experiences and platforms that resonate with consumers and contribute positively to society. Together, we are building brands that inspire confidence, fos-ter deeper connections, support responsible consumption, and create meaningful value for consumers, employees, artisans, partners, communities and shareholders.

Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) is at the 
forefront of India’s evolving fashion landscape, with a massive presence across over 900 towns and cities. Part of the Aditya Birla Group, headquartered in Mumbai, we operate a diver -
sified portfolio spanning value retail, ethnic wear, luxury and digital-first segments. 
The demerger marks the beginning of a transformative 
chapter for ABFRL, creating a more focused fashion and retail enterprise with sharper strategic priorities and greater agility to capitalize on India’s evolving consumption landscape. Built on decades of consumer trust, brand equity and retail excel-lence, we are uniquely positioned to accelerate growth across high-potential segments including value retail, ethnic wear, luxury fashion and digital-first brands. Our diverse portfolio of over 20 iconic brands, extensive retail footprint and omnichan-nel capabilities enable us to serve consumers across lifestyles, occasions and aspirations while strengthening long-term brand relevance and market leadership.

Sustainability 3.0: Advancing Responsible 
Fashion and Retail Growth
AS ABFRL ENTERS A NEW PHASE as a focused fashion 
and retail enterprise, Sustain-ability 3.0 strengthens our ambition to build brands that are not only admired for their style and innovation, but also trusted for the way they create value. Building on the strong foundations established through Sustainability 1.0 and 2.0, this next phase integrates sustainability more deeply into our brand strategy, retail operations, sourcing practices and consumer engagement, ensuring that growth and responsibility progress together.In an industry shaped by changing consumer aspirations, sustainability is increasingly becoming a differentiator for brands. Our diverse portfolio spanning value retail, eth-nic wear, luxury and digital-first businesses enables us to connect with consumers who expect fashion that reflects both personal expression and responsible choices. Sustain-ability 3.0 aligns our 2030 goals and 2050 aspirations with the Aditya Birla Group’s Purpose and Values, helping us strengthen brand relevance, enhance stakeholder trust and build resilience across our value chain.Through this approach, we are focused on creating fashion businesses that are future-ready, driven by responsible sourcing, resource-efficient operations, ethical supply chains and conscious consumption. By embedding sustainability into the way we design, manufacture, merchandise and re-tail our products, we seek to create differentiated consumer experiences while strengthening the long-term value and purpose of our brands.Our priorities are shaped by internal and external sustain-ability drivers that influence enterprise value, stakeholder expectations, and business resilience. Transition towards Sustainability 3.0
BUILDING RESILIENT, PURPOSE-LED FASHION BRANDSAligned with the Aditya Birla Group’s vision of creating sustainable businesses that deliver long-term value, ABFRL is advancing its sustainability journey to support its emer-gence as a focused fashion and retail powerhouse. In an increasingly dynamic global environment characterised by evolving consumer preferences, climate-related risks, supply chain disruptions, geopolitical uncertainty and changing regulatory expectations, we believe sustainability is a strategic lever for strengthening resilience, enhancing brand relevance and driving sustainable growth.
Our Sustainability 1.0 journey focused on establishing 
the foundations of responsible business practices. The emphasis was on strengthening governance, compliance, environmental management systems and resource ef -
ficiency across operations, creating the organisational discipline required to embed sustainability into business decision-making.
Building on this foundation, Sustainability 2.0 expanded 
the focus from operations to products and value chains. During this phase, we accelerated renewable energy adoption, strengthened responsible sourcing frameworks, enhanced ESG governance and disclosures, and integrated sustainability considerations into key business processes. This helped build operational resilience, improve stakehold -
er confidence and support the growth of our portfolio of fashion and lifestyle brands.
As we enter Sustainability 3.0, our ambition is to move 
beyond compliance and operational excellence towards 
creating competitive advantage through purpose-led growth. Sustainability is increasingly becoming a defining element of brand differentiation in the fashion industry, influencing consumer choice, investor con -
fidence and long-term business performance. Accordingly, we are embedding climate action, responsible products and inclu -
sive growth more deeply into our business strategy, operations and brand ecosystems.
This next phase focuses on 
building a more resilient and future-ready fashion business by integrating sustainability across the entire value chain, from prod-uct design, material selection and sourcing to manufacturing, retail operations, customer en-gagement and end-of-life considerations. We are strength -
ening our ability to respond to shifting market dynamics by reducing resource dependencies, improving supply chain resilience, expanding responsible sourcing practices and enhancing operational efficiency across our portfolio.
At the same time, Sustainability 3.0 positions our brands 
to respond to the growing demand for conscious con-sumption. By promoting responsible products, preserving traditional craftsmanship, supporting artisan communities and creating inclusive growth opportunities across our value chain, we are strengthening the social relevance and authenticity of our brands while creating shared value for stakeholders.
In a world marked by climate volatility, geopolitical 
uncertainty and rapidly changing consumer expectations, sustainability is increasingly becoming a critical driver of business continuity and resilience. It enables us to better manage risks, enhance adaptability, strengthen stakeholder trust and secure long-term competitiveness. Through Sus-tainability 3.0, we are not only reducing our environmental footprint but also building stronger brands, more resilient operations and deeper consumer connections, ensuring that ABFRL remains well-positioned to create lasting value while shaping the future of responsible fashion.
What Enabled the Transition
Our progress across governance, renewable energy adoption, responsible sourcing, safety systems, ESG disclosures, stake -
holder engagement, and operational efficiency has created a strong foundation for the next phase of our sustainability journey. These efforts have strengthened organisational read -
iness and enabled us to scale sustainability from operational initiatives to enterprise-wide transformation.
The Five Strategic Themes of Sustainability 3.0
1  Sustainable BrandsBuilding future-ready brands by integrating sustainability into brand purpose, consumer engagement, close-loop recycling initiatives, and measurable brand sustainability performance.
2 Product Stewardship
Driving responsible product ecosystems through sustainable raw materials, circularity, responsible sourcing, and supply chain sustainability while strengthening product transparen -
cy and eco-labelling practices.
3 Net Zero & Decarbonisation
Advancing our climate ambition by driving science-aligned emissions reduction across operations and the value chain.
4 Health, Safety & Well-being
Strengthening a culture of safety through a zero-harm mind -
set, predictive and digital safety excellence, and continuous learning and workforce enablement. We are committed to creating safe, healthy, and inclusive workplaces that support the well-being and development of our people.
5 Social Impact
Enabling inclusive growth by investing in Education, Health & Sanitation, Sustainable Livelihoods, Water & Watershed Management, and Digitalisation, while enhancing the long-term well-being of the communities we touch.
We further strengthen our social impact through em-
ployee volunteering initiatives, encouraging our people to contribute their skills, time, and expertise towards creating meaningful connections and positive change within commu -
nities.
Looking Ahead – Ambition 2030
Sustainability 3.0 reflects Aditya Birla Fashion’s ambition to lead the transition towards a more responsible, resilient, and future-ready fashion industry—creating long-term value for businesses, people, and the planet.
As we progress towards 2030, our focus will be on 
delivering measurable outcomes, accelerating innovation, and fostering collaboration across our value chain to ensure sustainability remains a key driver of growth, resilience, and stakeholder value creation.

Focused on priorities. Driven to going beyond.
FY 2025-26 marks a defining milestone in ABFRL’s journey. 
Following the demerger of the Madura Fashion & Lifestyle business, ABFRL has emerged as a more focused fashion and retail company, uniquely positioned to capture opportunities across some of the fastest-growing segments of the Indian fashion market, including value retail, ethnic wear, luxury fashion and digital-first brands. The strategic rationale be-hind the demerger was clear, i.e. to create sharper business focus, improve capital allocation, accelerate decision-making and enable each business to pursue distinct growth path-ways aligned with evolving consumer trends. Within this new structure, ABFRL is better equipped to leverage its differ-entiated portfolio, strengthen brand identities and deepen consumer engagement across multiple fashion categories.India’s fashion and lifestyle sector continues to be shaped by rising disposable incomes, increasing premiumisation, digital adoption and a growing preference for brands that align with consumer values. In this environment, competitive advantage is determined not only by product innovation and retail scale, but also by the ability to build trusted brands that remain relevant in a rapidly evolving marketplace. Our portfolio of iconic and emerging brands enables us to address diverse consumer aspirations across generations, occasions and price points while creating multiple engines of growth. Our stra-tegic priorities are therefore centred on strengthening brand equity, expanding our omnichannel ecosystem, enhancing customer experience and driving profitable, sustainable growth across our businesses.At the heart of our strategy is a commitment to building pur-pose-led brands. Masaba, Shantnu & Nikhil and TASVA, alongside the ongoing 
transformation of TCNS brands to strengthen their relevance in occasion wear.
With a scaled ethnic platform of over ₹2,200 crore in 
revenue and 680+ stores, we are well positioned to capture growth across high-value consumption segments.
The retail landscape is undergoing a significant trans-
formation driven by a generational shift that is redefining how commerce is experienced, how value is perceived and how brands evolve.  At the centre of this change is Gen Z: a digitally native, purpose-driven and highly influential consumer segment that is rapidly emerging as a key force in the market. Having grown up in a hyper-connected envi-ronment shaped by smartphones and social platforms, this cohort seeks more than products, prioritising personalisation, cultural relevance and seamless experiences across digital and physical touchpoints. For Indian and global retailers, this is a generational wake-up call to move beyond conventional formats and reimagine retail as dynamic, immersive, and socially connected. 
At ABFRL, we are strengthening our engagement with 
younger consumers across our portfolio through relevant design, accessible price points and enhanced digital inter-faces. This focus is reflected in the scaling of digital-first and value-led platforms such as TMRW and OWND, which are designed to capture trend-conscious, digitally native consumers through an omnichannel-first approach and rapid design-to-market capabilities. At the same time, we are leveraging our broader portfolio to build early consumer affinity and enhance lifetime value across younger cohorts, strengthening long-term growth.
The traditional distinctions between online and offline 
shopping experiences have blurred making omnichannel integration a strategic priority for apparel brands. Unlike multi-channel retailing, which operated through independent touchpoints, an omnichannel approach places the customer at the centre, enabling a cohesive, consistent and seamless experience across all channels. Retail journeys are increasing-ly becoming omnichannel, with consumers expecting seam-less interactions across stores, e-commerce platforms and digital touchpoints. Research on omnichannel adoption in In-dia identifies internet and smartphone penetration, changing consumer preferences, phygital shopping behaviour, AI-led personalisation, social commerce and supply chain optimis-ation as key drivers of this shift. A study focused on India’s apparel market also highlights omnichannel retailing as a response to changing consumer behaviour, where multiple purchase pathways and consistent brand interactions are becoming central to customer experience. 
Our omnichannel is a core pillar of our operating mod-
el, with increasing emphasis on deeper integration across physical stores, brand websites, marketplaces and supply chain systems. We are strengthening our ecosystem through investments in fulfilment capabilities, clienteling and digital infrastructure, enabling improved serviceability, faster deliv-ery and better inventory utilisation. We also leverage digital channels as a growth engine and a test-and-learn platform to refine our product and format strategies before scaling offline. This integrated approach enables us to enhance cus-tomer experience, improve operational efficiency and drive scalable growth across our diverse portfolio. 
The increasing convergence of technology, data and con-
sumer engagement is reshaping competitiveness in fashion and lifestyle retail. Research on AI-powered personalisation in online fashion retail shows that AI-enabled recommenda-tions, predictive analytics, chatbots and virtual assistance can improve customer experience, engagement and purchase decisions. 
We are advancing a unified “One ABFRL” digital eco-
system, supported by shared platforms and an integrated technology backbone. Core systems such as SAP S/4HANA, Dynamics 365 POS/CRM and a centralised e-commerce stack provide a single view of customers, inventory and performance, while enabling seamless integration across brands. In today’s increasingly complex and evolving business 
environment, uncertainty remains an inherent challenge. Recognising these complexities, organisations are required to navigate shifting market dynamics, regulatory changes, supply chain disruptions, and emerging threats such as geo-political tensions and climate change. At ABFRL, we adopt a proactive approach to risk management by embedding forward looking strategies that strengthen operational resil-ience. By anticipating potential risks, we enhance our ability to mitigate risks manage them effectively mitigate risks while adapting to evolving conditions and ensuring business continuity.
Risk Governance Structure 
Our risk governance framework is anchored in the three lines of defense model, ensuring comprehensive oversight and accountability.
Under this model, responsibility for risk management 
is distributed across defined layers. Operational teams and business leaders form the first line, owning the identification and management of risks in day to day operations. The sec-ond line comprises dedicated risk and compliance functions at the senior management level, tasked to establish policies, define risk control frameworks, and monitor adherence to ensure risks are managed within defined boundaries. The third line is the independent internal audit function, which provides objective assurance on the effectiveness of risk controls, governance, and compliance practices across the organisation. Together, these layers enable coordinated over-sight and strengthen our ability to manage risks effectively.
Risk Management Process
At ABFRL, we have underpinned a strategically aligned Risk Management Framework to proactively manage and miti-gate business risks in alignment with COSO’s enterprise risk management principles. Guided by our Risk Management Policy, a dedicated team ensures effective implementation, with continuous monitoring of emerging risks. The frame-work defines the company’s risk appetite, the level of risk it is willing to accept for identified risks. Our independent assurance mechanisms further reinforce risk governance. We conduct annual internal audits to review adherence to risk management frameworks and compliance requirements, with additional evaluation of effectiveness and regulatory align-ment by annual external audit.The Board-level Risk management and Sustainability Com-mittee actively exercises the oversight of this framework, ensuring strategic alignment and robust risk governance.
Risk Identification & Categorization
We systematically undertake a structured and rigorous eval-uation of risks and classify them across strategic, operational, financial, environmental, and compliance-related domains,

Mitigation and Control Measures
Building on the assessment outcomes, suitable risk control 
measures are put in place, with corrective actions embedded into standard operating procedures to prevent recurrence. This proactive approach strengthens organisational agility and supports effective response to evolving uncertainties.
Continuous Monitoring and Review
At ABFRL, our risk assessments are conducted at regular in-tervals, with urgent reviews undertaken as needed to address emerging risks and strengthen resilience. Where necessary, immediate reviews are conducted to ensure timely mitigation of potential risks. The framework is also subject to annual internal audits, supporting continuous improvement and readiness.
The Risk Management and Sustainability Committee 
meet twice a year to oversee the identification, assessment, and mitigation and provide strategic direction and oversight across the economic, social, and environmental risk dimen-sions. This includes reviewing risk exposure and ensuring a structured response to emerging challenges.
Increasing Risk Awareness
As part of ongoing board and committee meetings, indepen-dent and non executive directors are regularly apprised of key developments through structured presentations covering business operations, strategy, risk management framework, industry trends, and regulatory updates. Additionally, risk focused sessions are also conducted for the Board whenever significant revisions occur and is further extended to func-tional heads of new businesses to ensure a strong under-standing across leadership. 
As a part of the onboarding process, employees undergo 
comprehensive training on key risk areas such as safety, sus-tainability, information security, and legal compliance. This is further supplemented by role specific training programmes, including occupational health and safety for relevant teams, reinforcing a culture of proactive risk management through-out the organisation.
Through regular engagement with stakeholders, the governance body gains insights and feedback that help in understanding the concerns and expectations of various stakeholders. 
This process ensures that the governance body remains 
well-informed about the potential impacts and associated risks. By incorporating stakeholder perspectives, the gover-nance body can make more informed decisions, effectively manage risks, and seize opportunities that align with stake-holder interests and contribute to sustainable development. Inputs from respective process owners who provide quar-terly risk updates help identify potential risks that they may perceive. In addition, clear mechanism for reporting value violations, ethics non-compliance and whistle blower policies are in place encouraging employees to report any risks they may observe through these channels.
Integrating Risk Management in  
Product Development  
Product development at ABFRL follows a structured process 
that incorporates risk management at every stage, enabling innovation while addressing potential risks. Through cross functional collaboration, we co develop concepts and de-signs, drawing on diverse perspectives to strengthen product viability. By embedding risk considerations throughout devel-opment, we ensure our products remain robust, efficient, and aligned with business priorities and market needs.
More details on identified risks, corresponding mitigation 
measures, and emerging opportunities are provided in the ‘Management Discussion and Analysis’ section of the report.considering their likelihood and magnitude. Through a de-tailed root cause analysis, we assess their potential impli-cations on business operations, enabling prudent and data driven decision making.
Risk Assessment & Prioritisation
Once identified, risks are plotted on a heat map based on their likelihood and severity, and classified as high (red), me-dium (amber), or low (green). This approach helps prioritise actions and focus mitigation efforts to safeguard business resilience. We evaluate risks at both gross and net levels to refine our risk evaluation process. Gross risk represents the inherent exposure in the current business environment be-fore controls are applied, while net risk reflects the mitigated impact after risk management actions.
Alongside direct risks, we also assess both upside and 
downside scenarios. Upside risk relates to missed opportuni-ties for growth, cost savings, and innovation, while downside risk encompasses adverse negative outcomes such as finan-

GEOECONOMIC 
CONFRONTATION Deployment of economic levers by global or regional powers to reshape economic interactions between nations, restricting goods, knowledge, services or technology with the intent of building self-sufficiency, constraining geopolitical rivals and/or consolidating spheres of influence. These leads to significant increase in the prices of the exports, impact the availability, costing and movement of raw materials. Geoeconomic confrontation can disrupt supply chains through tariffs, sanctions, and trade restrictions, leading to higher sourcing costs and limited access to materials and suppliers. This may impact inventory availability, delay product launches, and pressure margins in a competitive retail environment.As part of our focus on supply chain resilience, we are building stronger partnerships with MSME suppliers, Indian vendors, and nearby manufacturers to support localised sourcing. Additionally, we are incorporating fibres made in-house by the Aditya Birla Group, such as Birla Cellulose LIVA Eco Fibre, reducing dependence on external suppliers and reinforcing production continuity.
MISINFORMATION AND DISINFORMATIONThere is a risk of false or misleading information relating to product quality, brand authenticity, responsible sourcing, sustainability claims, and circularity initiatives. In a digital-first retail environment, such information can spread rapidly and influence consumer sentiment and purchasing behaviour. Proactive communication, transparency, and responsible marketing are essential to safeguard stakeholder trust.Misinformation and disinformation can affect consumer trust, damage brand reputation, and disrupt customer loyalty. Misleading narratives around product attributes, sourcing practices, sustainability performance, or circularity initiatives may result in stakeholder confusion, allegations of greenwashing, regulatory scrutiny, and legal consequences. Brand impersonation and fabricated content may also influence purchasing decisions and dilute brand identity.We uphold responsible marketing practices by ensuring transparency, accuracy, and fairness across customer communications. Product, sustainability, and circularity claims are appropriately reviewed and supported by relevant evidence. We monitor digital channels for misleading content and brand impersonation and take corrective action, where required. Clear product labelling and consistent communication help safeguard consumer trust and reinforce brand integrity.
ADOPTION TO RAPIDLY EVOLVING AI TECHNOLOGYThe rapid evolution of AI technology presents opportunities to enhance operational efficiency, innovation, decision-making and customer experience. However, keeping pace with emerging capabilities requires timely adoption, reliable data, appropriate infrastructure, skilled resources and effective governance. Delayed or ineffective adoption may limit the ability to realise business value and remain competitive in a rapidly changing retail environment.Gaps in the adoption and integration of AI across merchandise planning, markdown management, design assistance, e-commerce automation and customer engagement may result in missed opportunities, process inefficiencies and reduced competitiveness. Inadequate system integration, employee readiness or oversight may also affect output accuracy, operational reliability and decision-making, leading to financial and reputational risks.We follow a structured approach to AI adoption, supported by robust governance, human oversight and data protection controls. AI solutions are evaluated for business relevance, accuracy, reliability and security before deployment, with appropriate oversight maintained during their use. Employee training, capability-building and assessment of emerging technologies support the responsible, secure and effective adoption of AI.

Recognising the significance of risks, opportunities and 
sustainability impacts, we undertook a comprehensive double materiality assessment in FY 2023–24. We review our material topics annually to remain responsive to evolving business landscape and stakeholder expectations. To ensure our material topics remain closely aligned with evolving busi-ness objectives and stakeholder priorities, we have initiated a detailed materiality assessment, which will be completed in FY 2026–27.
The assessment process involved engagement with a 
broad range of internal and external stakeholders, including senior management, employees, customers, academia, in-dustry bodies, CSR partners, investors, suppliers, franchisees, and service providers. Through this engagement, we identi-fied actual and potential impacts of our business activities on the economy, environment, and society.
The approach was supported by sectoral research, market 
intelligence, and peer benchmarking to evaluate impacts across the short, medium, and long term. Using structured qualitative methodologies, material topics were systemati-cally mapped on a materiality matrix to enable prioritisation and strategic alignment.
The outcomes of the assessment were reviewed and ap-
proved by the Board of Directors and further validated by an independent third party. The identified material topics have since been integrated into our Risk Management Framework, ensuring a coordinated and proactive approach to address-ing key sustainability priorities.

Resource 
management Energy and water Opportunity and RiskThe fashion industry, known for its high levels of waste, pollution, and resource consumption, is seen as a major contributor to climate change. Excessive and inefficient use of resources can lead to higher operational costs, regulatory penalties, and negative environmental impacts, damaging brand reputation.However, efficient resource usage and focus on raw materials and processes with lower environmental impact can result in cost savings, increased customer loyalty, the opening of new market segments and a stronger brand image.We are redesigning our products to increase wardrobe life, reduce environmental impact and enable reuse at their end-of-life stage.Through our Sustainable Attributes, Sustainable Supplier Index and global assessment frameworks such as the Higg Index, we integrate sustainability across product life cycle and value chain. We also strengthen resource efficiency across operations through energy and water management measures such as solar rooftop systems, biomass briquettes, EV forklifts, rainwater harvesting, reuse of treated water from STPs, water-efficient fixtures and water positive projects.Positive GRI 302: Energy 2016

Climate ChangeRisk The carbon footprint of a garment largely depends on the material. While synthetic fibres like polyester have less impact on water and land than grown materials like cotton, they emit more greenhouse gases per kilogram.It is crucial to effectively manage emissions from across the value chain to limit the potential negative impact of climate changeWe have adopted various initiatives across Scope 1 & 2 emissions and initiated dialogue with stake-holders for mitigating Scope 3 emissions across the value chain.We are enhancing the share of re-newable energy and reducing our carbon and water footprint at both facility and product levels to effectively address climate change and its impacts.We have a target to utilise renewable energy to run all of our operational facilities and achieve a 5.5% YoY reduction in Scope 1 & 2.Negative GRI 305: Emissions 2016• Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions• GHG emissions intensity• Reduction of GHG emissions• Emissions of ozone-depleting substances (ODS)Natural Capital
Waste Management and Circular Economy
Risk The repercussions of fast fashion are multi-faceted and need to be monitored closely. It contributes to significant pollution, resource depletion, and textile waste, with vast amounts of clothing ending up in landfills, leading to increased scrutiny from regulators.It becomes crucial to effectively manage this waste and adopt the circular economy approach to maintain a positive brand image and gain customer loyalty.We continued to accelerate the transition from linear to circular models by integrating circular principles in our own operations and across the value chain.We are aiming to achieve ‘Zero Waste to Landfill’ by 2030.The entire non-hazardous waste in our facilities is either recycled or reused, and a small quantity undergoes composting, which is used as bio manure for farming.Our collaboration with Germany’s GIZ focuses on material innovation, reducing inputs of harmful substances, increasing textile-to-textile recycling, developing alternatives to plastic packaging, and fostering traceability.We have undertaken a commitment to recycle or upcycle 10% of products by volume

Our Company delivered a robust performance in FY26, 
marked by double-digit revenue growth and steady improve-ment in profitability. Revenue grew by 11% year-on-year to ₹8,177 crore, supported by strong momentum across key business segments, disciplined execution and continued operational improvements across the portfolio.
The Ethnic business delivered double-digit growth, while 
TMRW continued to scale at a high growth rate. Pantaloons maintained a steady and consistent performance during the year. Retail and e-commerce channels also registered robust growth, driven by healthy LTL growth, improved execution and stronger consumer engagement across formats.
Our Company remains focused on driving operating effi-
ciencies by leveraging its strong backend capabilities across sourcing and manufacturing, retail execution and digital integration. These capabilities continue to support better agility, improved productivity and sharper execution across the business.
Our Company also continues to strengthen its om-
ni-channel ecosystem by seamlessly integrating its physical store network with brand websites, marketplaces and other digital platforms. This approach is guided by the under-standing that each brand operates at a different stage of its growth lifecycle and therefore requires a tailored distribu-tion strategy with distinct channel priorities. At the overall Company level, calibrated store expansion continued across priority markets, with the addition of over 180 new stores during FY 2025-26. The overall retail footprint witnessed a net increase of ~0.6 million sq. ft., taking the total retail space to 7.9 million sq. ft. as on March 31, 2026.
In line with evolving consumer preferences, the Company 
launched new formats during the year, including Galeries Lafayette in luxury retail and OWND, targeted at Gen Z consumers. These launches reflect the Company’s continued focus on expanding into high-potential consumption spaces and building future-ready growth platforms.
Our capital allocation strategy remains focused on 
strengthening growth platforms and scaling brand portfolio. As on March 31, 2026, we maintained a standalone gross cash balance of ₹1,150 crore, providing adequate liquidity to support its growth priorities. Subsidiaries, including design-er-led brands and TMRW, are expected to continue funding their own growth requirements.
Pantaloons Segment
In line with the fast evolving masstige and value fashion segment, Pantaloons has been on a strategic transformation journey centered on premiumization, superior merchandising, enhanced store experiences with a customer proposition of a stronger self-expression led fashion. Our strategic initiatives are now reflecting in our growth trajectory with Q4 FY26 recording one -of its highest growth performance. 
Pantaloons delivered a steady performance with revenue 
of ₹4560 Cr in FY26, a growth of 4% over previous year, amid 
challenging environment. Company continued to optimize its store network while enhancing its in-store retail experience, with its store count reducing to 399 while footprint increased to 5,781 000’ sq.ft.  
During the year, company rebranded Style-Up as OWND 
with the objective of building the right customer base, enhancing store productivity and accelerating digital led customer acquisitions. It is currently in investment phase, and continues to strengthen its presence with its store network expanding to 79 stores as on 31 March 2026. 
EBITDA was at ₹739 Cr, with EBITDA margin of 16.2%, 
despite the impact of continued ramp-up in OWND. 
Outlook: As leaders in masstige and value fashion, we 
continue to drive future growth in this segment through 
Pantaloons. We are steadfast on improving productivity and margin expansion along with calibrated store expansion with an omni-channel distribution strategy.  The company believes OWND business is shaping up as expected and is well-poised to seize the emerging opportunities in this intensely compet -
itive space.

Following a  successful demerger,, we embraced a  more

At the core of this approach is our Product Sustainability 
Attribute framework, which provides a simple way to evalu-ate how sustainable each product is. It is based on five key criteria that consider both environmental and social impacts across the product’s lifecycle. In FY 2025–26, approximately 95% of the product portfolio met at least one sustainability attribute, while 80% have two sustainable attributes, indicat-ing a gradual shift towards deeper integration of sustainabil-ity across product lines. To bring this story to life for internal stakeholders, we continue to leverage our Brand Sustainabil-ity Dashboard, a dynamic Management Information System that translates data into insights. 
As we move forward as an independent entity, our vision 
is to create products that resonate with evolving consumer expectations while contributing to a more resilient fashion ecosystem. The path ahead will be defined by continuous innovation, stronger accountability, and a commitment to scaling impact. In doing so, we reaffirm that sustainability is an ongoing journey, where every product tells a story of responsibility, progress, and purpose.

Leading Product Sustainability
Over the course of our decade-long ReEarth sustainability journey, we repositioned our products  as the primary vehicle for environmental and social value creation, as we transi-tioned from a process-led to a product-led sustainability model, representing one of the most consequential structural MANUFACTURED CAPITAL

This approach not only preserves traditional knowledge systems but also supports inclusive livelihoods and culturally rooted production models. In parallel, we have significantly strengthened the sustainability of packaging ecosystem, achieving 99.8% sustainable packaging material usage at pantaloons, through initiatives such as compostable poly-bags, the integration of plastic-free packaging components, and the elimination of plastic carry bags across Pantaloons stores, reducing material consumption and advancing circu-larity across our retail operations.

integrating FSC®-certified and traceable Liva Eco™ viscose across Women’s Ethnic, Western and Kidswear portfolios. Through this transition, the brand shifted approximately 9 lakh metres from conventional viscose to more responsible forest-based fibre alternatives, improving traceability and reducing sourcing-related risks.
Together, these initiatives highlight Pantaloons’ focus on 
improving its operations, packaging, supplier network and product capabilities. By combining efficient infrastructure with responsible material choices, the brand is building a more sustainable and future-ready retail model.
