› Driving Brand Sustainability
› JAYPORE — TO DRIVE OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY and sustainability across its supply chain, Jaypore imple-
mented a series of initiatives focused on resource optimi-sation, green logistics and responsible packaging. Under a shared-services model, Jaypore allocated 9,000 sq. ft. of warehouse space within its Noida Distribution Centre to SNN, improving infrastructure utilisation, enabling resource shar-ing, avoiding duplication of warehousing assets and generat-ing an annual financial impact of approximately ₹45 lakh.
As part of its Green Logistics Initiative, Jaypore intro-
duced electric vehicles for NCR store deliveries through a logistics partner, supported by charging infrastructure at the warehouse. The initiative reduced dependence on conven-tional fuel-based transportation and lowered the carbon emissions.
Jaypore also undertook a comprehensive Packaging 
Transformation Programme after identifying the extensive use of non-sustainable and multi-layer packaging materials across warehouse operations. Key interventions included the replacement of polyethylene bags with certified compostable alternatives, reduction of packaging layers across apparel, jewellery and footwear categories, and consolidation of mul-tiple product tags into a single integrated tag with QR-en-abled product information. To further strengthen circularity, a carton shredder was installed at the Noida warehouse to convert used corrugated cartons into honeycomb cushioning material, replacing thermocol and foam-based fillers. These measures significantly reduced packaging waste, lowered material consumption and generated cost savings, while supporting circular economy practices.
The initiatives delivered significant financial, environmen-
tal and operational benefits for Jaypore. Packaging optimis-ation generated estimated monthly savings of approximately ₹1.72 lakh, including savings of ₹20.75 per apparel unit and ₹5.25 per jewellery unit. Jaypore eliminated poly bags from its B2C dispatch stream, reduced non-sustainable content in apparel packaging to less than 1%, and significantly lowered corrugation waste through the use of lightweight paper bags. Operationally, the initiatives simplified packaging processes, reduced packing cycle time, reduced operational waste, and strengthened alignment with ESG commitments and EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) requirements.

› Driving Brand Sustainability
Reimagining Rare Crafts for Contemporary Consumers — 
Jaypore’s Tangaliya Journey
Jaypore’s rare crafts programme focuses on preserving traditional craft techniques while reimagining them for con-
temporary consumers. The brand’s Design, Product and Sourcing teams identify rare craft clusters, study their supply ecosystems and develop season-agnostic products with longer lead times to protect the integrity of slow, intricate 
craft processes. Jaypore is currently working with around 6–8 rare craft clusters 
across apparel and home products, with the aim of launching at least one rare craft every year.
Tangaliya, a rare handwoven craft from Gujarat’s Surendranagar region, has 
been a key focus since 2021. Practised by a limited number of skilled weavers from the Dangasia community, the craft is known for its raised dana dots created direct-ly on the loom. After its first launch in 2021, Jaypore relaunched Tangaliya in 2025 as a lighter cotton-silk kurta set with a contemporary motif language suited for festive wear. The collection became one of Jaypore’s festive bestsellers, achieving 57% sell-through.
The initiative supports one core master weaver, his weaver unit and women 
artisans involved in yarn preparation, finishing and pre/post-weaving activities. Through Karigari Ki Kahani, Jaypore amplified the craft story across digital, social, retail and PR platforms. For Spring Summer 2027, Jaypore plans to further devel-op Tangaliya through new yarn types, textures, hand feel and drape, converting it into a planned seasonal craft pipeline.Dokra: Reviving an Ancient Metal Craft
Through Karigari Ki Kahani (KKK), Jaypore brings the stories of Indian crafts to a wider world celebrating the makers, materials, and traditions that shape the country’s rich artisanal heritage. Rooted in immersive storytelling and mean-ingful cultural engagement, the initiative creates deeper consumer connections while honouring the communities behind every handcrafted creation.
As part of this ongoing endeavour, Jaypore spotlighted Dokra, one of India’s oldest metal-casting traditions, 
practised by artisan communities across eastern and central India using the centuries-old lost-wax casting technique. Under the broader theme of ‘Concept to Creators to Consumers’, the initiative traced the journey of Dokra from an 
artisan’s imagination to a finished handcrafted object, highlighting the skill, patience and generational knowledge that sustain this unique craft tradition.
Through rich visual storytelling, artisan-led narratives and immersive retail experienc-
es, Jaypore helped decode the intricate craftsmanship of Dokra for modern consumers while drawing attention to the importance of preserving traditional and vulnerable craft forms. Reinforcing its role as a curator and storyteller of Indian craft heritage, Jaypore brought the essence of Dokra alive across its stores, where culturally rooted design elements are thoughtfully blended with contemporary aesthetics. Inspired by the warmth and spatial language of traditional Indian homes, these immersive environments enabled consumers to engage with the craft beyond the product, fostering a deeper appreciation of India’s living artisanal traditions.

We are driven by a bold vision to create a workplace 
where talent is not only supported but amplified. By thoughtfully attracting, developing, and nurturing exception-al individuals, we foster a progressive and inclusive ecosys-tem where diverse perspectives thrive, innovation is encour-aged, and learning remains continuous and future-focused.

At ABFRL, we do more than compete for talent we create 
an ecosystem where exceptional talent chooses to belong and thrive. We are committed to building a workplace where individuals are empowered to shape their own journeys and realise their full potential.
We offer an environment where opportunities are expan-
sive across brands, functions, and geographies enabling our people to explore diverse pathways and build meaningful, future-ready careers. We encourage ownership of growth, supported by leaders who listen actively, mentor with intent, and are willing to invest in and champion bold potential.
Learning is embedded into the fabric of our organisation, 
ensuring our people continuously build capabilities that pre-pare them for evolving business needs and future leadership roles. At the same time, we foster a culture of real-time ap-preciation, where achievements both significant milestones and everyday contributions are recognised and celebrated.
We also believe that sustained performance is rooted in 
holistic well-being. By creating an environment where work and life coexist in harmony, we prioritise flexibility, inclusiv-ity, and a strong sense of belonging, enabling our people to thrive both professionally and personally.
By bringing together a compelling employer brand, a 
differentiated Employee Value Proposition, and meaningful growth opportunities, we continue to strengthen our position as a destination of choice for top talent. We are building a workplace where individuals do not simply work they grow, lead, innovate, and leave a lasting impact on the future of fashion and retail.We recognise that our ability to attract and 
retain the right talent is fundamental to building a resilient and future-ready organisation. We are deeply committed to fostering an inclusive workplace, welcoming individuals from diverse nationalities, backgrounds, and identities, as we believe that diversity strengthens our culture, enhances creativity, and drives innovation. Guided by the Aditya Birla Group’s Corporate Principles and Code of Conduct, we uphold the highest standards of fairness, integrity, and respect across all our people practices.
Our workforce planning is strongly anchored 
in our internal business priorities, which act as the primary drivers of our talent strategy. As 
we continue to expand across brands, formats, and geogra-phies, there is a growing need to scale capabilities across our corporate, retail, warehouse, sampling units and manufac-turing facilities. The rapid advancement of our omnichannel and digital ecosystem has further accelerated demand for new-age skills, while ongoing business transformation has reshaped capability requirements across functions. At the same time, we remain focused on driving productivity and cost optimisation, ensuring that our workforce remains effi-cient and ready for the future. Strengthening our leadership pipeline and building succession depth across critical roles also remain our key internal priorities, enabling long-term organisational resilience.
These internal drivers are complemented by external 
market realities, including a dynamic retail landscape marked by evolving consumer preferences and intense competition for specialised and digital talent. Together, these factors shape a responsive and forward-looking workforce strategy.
In line with this, we have continued to refine our talent 
approach to attract high-potential individuals across levels and generations. During the reporting year, we adopted a ho-listic and business-aligned hiring strategy, with a deliberate shift towards a more structured and technology-enabled re-cruitment model, leveraging AI-driven tools and behavioural assessments to enhance effectiveness. We maintained a balanced focus on lateral, leadership, and early-career hiring, while also emphasising critical and emerging capabilities such as digital, analytics, supply chain, and design. We also advanced our diversity hiring agenda and reinforced internal pipelines through robust succession planning and enhanced internal mobility opportunities.
We take a proactive and highly structured approach to 
managing critical talent attrition, with a focused emphasis on high performers and roles that are pivotal to business continuity. Our approach begins with the systematic identi-fication of risks through regular talent reviews, supported by workforce analytics and attrition trend analysis. We clearly map critical roles and high-potential talent pools to ensure focused attention, while continuous feedback mechanisms such as engagement surveys and manager insights enable us to stay closely aligned with employee sentiment. Building on these insights, we implement targeted retention initiatives designed to create a differentiated and compelling employee experience. This includes offering customised compensation and reward frameworks for high performers, investing signifi-cantly in career development, learning pathways, and lead-ership capability building, and actively promoting internal mobility and cross-functional opportunities to enrich career journeys. In parallel, we continue to strengthen employ-ee-centric initiatives with a strong emphasis on well-being, engagement, and an enabling work environment, ensuring that our people feel valued, supported, and motivated to stay and grow with the organisation.
Nurturing Young Talent : Stride – Young Talent 
Management Programme 
The STRIDE Programme is Aditya Birla Fashion’s flagship 
young talent initiative, designed to identify, develop, and nurture future leaders for the organisation. What began over two decades ago with the induction of Business Management Trainees (BMTs) has evolved into a robust, multi-disciplinary talent pipeline that today includes Fashion Management Trainees (FMTs), Chartered Accountant (CA) Striders, and B.Tech/M.Tech Striders. The programme continues to expand its reach by strengthening relationships with leading cam-puses across the country while continuously evaluating and onboarding new institutes to build a diverse and future-ready talent pool.
Today, the STRIDE community comprises over 270 
Striders across multiple batches, streams, and business units, making it one of the organisation’s most enduring talent pipelines. Managed centrally, the program ensures consistent and enriching employee experience through structured learn-ing interventions, cross-functional exposure, mentoring, and continuous career development. Guided by the philosophy of “Once a Strider, Always a Strider,” every participant remains connected to the program throughout their journey, with a dedicated HR team partnering with them at every stage of their career.
The success of the STRIDE Program is reflected in the 
journeys of its alumni. Many former management trainees have grown into leadership roles and today lead key func-tions and businesses across Aditya Birla Fashion, reinforcing the program’s role in building a strong internal leadership pipeline. As the organisation continues to evolve, STRIDE remains committed to attracting high-potential talent, fos-tering innovation and agility, and developing leaders who will shape the future of Aditya Birla Fashion.
Our investment in talent acquisition remained strong and 
deliberate, with a total hiring spend of ₹4.1 crore, reflecting our continued focus on attracting high-calibre professionals who align with our vision and values. During FY 2025–26, we welcomed 6,451 new employees into the organisation, of which 40% were women, reinforcing our sustained commit-ment to enhancing gender diversity across all levels. Building a Future-Ready Leadership Pipeline 
At ABFRL, we firmly believe that organisations that succeed over the long term are those that invest early in building their future leaders. Strengthening our leadership pipeline remains a strategic priority, and our Talent Councils play a pivotal role in ensuring leadership continuity through a structured and forward-looking approach to identifying, developing, and positioning talent for critical roles.  
We leverage a robust 9-box performance–potential 
framework, further validated through Emerging Councils (JB 6–9) and Leadership Councils (JB 4–5), to systematically identify high-potential talent and align them with future organisational needs. Through this process, we actively map talent to opportunities, create bridge roles, and establish clearly defined succession plans for key positions. This disci-plined and proactive approach ensures that every strategic role is supported by ready-now or ready-soon successors, enabling ABFRL to operate with agility, resilience, and confi-dence as we scale.
Our performance management philosophy is designed to 
be holistic, inclusive, and developmental. We have adopted multi-dimensional appraisal mechanisms, including 360-de-gree feedback, allowing employees to receive well-round-ed, constructive insights from multiple stakeholders. This is complemented by a culture of continuous feedback, where regular conversations between managers and team members support real-time performance improvement and development. We also emphasise team-based performance assessment, recognising the importance of collaboration and collective outcomes alongside individual contributions.
Through these integrated efforts, we are not only 
strengthening our leadership bench but also fostering a culture of accountability, growth, and sustained high perfor-mance across the organisation.
 
Planned Actions to Strengthen Retention
We believe that talent must not only be attracted and developed but also meaningfully retained through enriching employee experiences and visible growth opportunities. Our focus is on building a workplace where ambition is matched with a strong sense of belonging, enabling every individual to envision a long-term future with us. During the year, our voluntary employee turnover stood at 19.24%, and in re-sponse, we are taking deliberate steps to further strengthen retention outcomes. We are enhancing career pathing frame-works to provide greater transparency and clarity on growth opportunities across roles and functions, while also expand-ing internal mobility avenues to encourage cross-functional exposure and career progression. 
We continue to invest in strengthening managerial 
effectiveness, recognising the critical role leaders play in shaping employee experience and engagement. At the same time, we are deepening our focus on continuous learning, reskilling, and building future-ready capabilities to keep our workforce relevant and resilient. Leveraging people analytics and AI-driven insights, we aim to adopt a more predictive and data-led approach to retention and workforce planning, enabling us to proactively address potential risks and rein-force a culture where our people feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow with us.

A Promise of Growth and Belonging
Our Employee Value Proposition (EVP) goes beyond a 
statement—it is a commitment we bring to life every day. It is thoughtfully anchored in four core pillars that reflect the diverse aspirations of our people and shape a workplace where individuals feel supported, inspired, and empowered to succeed.
Career: We offer expansive opportunities for individuals 
to explore, grow, and evolve within the organisation and across the Aditya Birla Group. Our strong culture of mobility reflects in internal role movements, enabling employees to build dynamic, fluid careers that extend beyond traditional boundaries.
Learning & Development: We cultivate a culture of con-
tinuous learning through structured programmes, immersive academies, and Elev8 our University of Growth. This ecosys-tem fosters lifelong learning, equipping our people with the capabilities required for present-day excellence and future leadership.
Reward & Recognition: Our multi-layered reward and 
recognition framework ensures that excellence is consistently acknowledged. By embedding recognition into everyday practices, we create an environment where contributions are valued in real time rather than confined to periodic reviews.
Enrich Your Life: We recognise the importance of balance 
and well-being and strive to create an environment where professional and personal aspirations coexist harmoniously. Through flexible policies, well-being initiatives, and platforms for connection and self-expression, we support the holistic growth of every individual.
Through this integrated EVP, we ensure that every em-

It is awarded only after a compre-hensive, independent audit that evaluates how organisations perform across the most critical dimensions of workplace gender equity. The Certification places us among a select group of

Well-Being without Boundaries

al resilience, mental readiness, gratitude, and overall mental health awareness. With over 450 employee responses across sessions and surveys, the programme continues to play a key role in normalising conversations around mental health beyond traditional support mechanisms.
We have also strengthened our preventive health -
care focus through the Annual Health Check-up (AHC) programme. Following a successful pilot in Mumbai, the initiative was scaled across locations, achieving 99.8% completion in Mumbai and 77% completion across the rest of India during the year. Delivered through a network of over 156 centres, the programme was supported by strong communication and on-ground facilitation. Employee feed -
back reflects high satisfaction levels, with 89% rating the experience as good or very good, 93% acknowledging its effectiveness for health and well-being, and 91% highlight -
ing ease of access and booking.
Our well-being initiatives are underpinned by a da -

Employee Benefits 
We take a holistic approach to employee well-being, with a 
strong focus on health, security, and work–life integration. Our comprehensive benefits includes health and accident insurance, as well as life insurance coverage for all employ-ees and workers, with claims facilitated through EDLI under EPFO, ensuring financial protection and peace of mind.
We also support employees through key life stages with 
progressive parental policies, including 26 weeks of ma-ternity leave and 5 days of paternity leave, reinforcing our commitment to family well-being. Complementing this, we offer childcare and daycare facilities, lactation support, and flexible working arrangements, work from home options, enabling employees to balance professional responsibilities with personal commitments.
To further promote overall well-being, we invest in stress 
management programmes, sports and fitness initiatives, and wellness-driven activities that encourage healthy lifestyles. Together, these initiatives create a supportive and inclusive ecosystem where employees can thrive, both at work and beyond.
The long-term incentive programmes, including stock 
options and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), extend to em-ployees below senior management, with approximately 40% coverage and an average vesting period of three years.  This approach enables our people to actively participate in the organisation’s long-term value creation, fostering a strong sense of ownership and shared success.
We recognise that the future of Human Resources lies 
beyond transactional processes it is fundamentally experien-tial. Through a thoughtfully designed HR service model, we are shaping a seamless and intuitive employee experience, underpinned by digital transformation, robust governance structures, comprehensive benefits, and data-driven deci-sion-making.
A Culture of Recognition and Appreciation 
We do not treat recognition as a periodic exercise. How-
ever, it is embedded deeply within our culture and reflected in everyday interactions, milestones, and achievements. We believe that when people feel genuinely valued, they are inspired to perform at their best, innovate with confidence, and build a lasting sense of belonging. Our Rewards and Rec -
ognition (R&R) ecosystem is therefore thoughtfully designed to celebrate excellence in all its forms whether it is break-through achievements, consistent contributions, exceptional teamwork, or long-standing commitment.
We have built a multi-layered recognition framework that 
ensures every employee, across levels and geographies, feels seen and valued:Pat on the Back:
At the core of our approach is every day and monthly recog-nition, where appreciation is immediate and visible. 1.Coaching for Cultural Transformation – Building Leaders Who Unlock Potential Culture shifts when leaders change how they lead. Our Coaching for Cultural Transformation initiative is an eight-month, ICF-accredited certification programme that embeds coaching as a core leadership behaviour at ABFRL. Through a structured journey of mind-fulness practices, deep listening, and powerful questioning techniques, participants develop the ability to guide, support, and inspire their teams more effectively. The programme empowers leaders to foster a culture of growth, continuous development, and high performance, enabling every indi-vidual to bring their best self to work and realise their full potential. 
2.Enterprise Risk Management Training – Strengthening 
Agile and Responsible Leadership In a dynamic, ever-chang-ing market, risk awareness is not optional it is a leadership imperative. Our Enterprise Risk Management Training is a two-day, classroom-based, experiential learning intervention designed to build robust risk assessment and mitigation capabilities among leaders. Through action-based exercises, case studies, and real-life scenario planning, participants learn to identify, assess, and proactively manage enter-prise-level risks. This capability strengthens decision-making agility, reinforces governance excellence, and builds resilience within our leadership pipeline— ensuring we stay ahead of challenges while driving sustainable growth.
3.Being a Mentor – Creating a Culture of Shared Growth 
and Guidance We believe great cultures are shaped by leaders who lift others as they rise. Our Being a Mentor pro-gramme equips employees with the skills to nurture talent, share wisdom, and inspire the next generation of leaders. This two-day virtual intervention, supported by reference videos, hands-on exercises, and real-world application scenarios, builds self-awareness, sharpens communication skills, and enhances interpersonal effectiveness. By the end of the programme, participants are confident and competent mentors, able to guide others meaningfully while reinforcing our culture of learning and collaboration. 
4.Managerial Effectiveness – Empowering Leaders to 
Decide, Delegate, and Deliver Our Managerial Effectiveness programme is an initiative aimed at strengthening deci-sion-making agility, coaching capabilities, and team manage-ment effectiveness among our middle-management cadre. The programme focuses on connecting meaningfully with teams, implementing the GROW coaching model, delegating effectively using FIRO-B learnings, and driving structured team reviews through well-defined agendas, clear account-ability, and consistent review cadences. 
5.Retirement Transition Programme – Supporting Life Be-
yond the Workplace We see leadership as a lifelong journey, not just a career phase. The Turning a New Leaf – Planning for Retirement programme, under the ABG Gyanodaya initia-tive, supports senior managers approaching retirement with tools, reflections, and planning frameworks to navigate this important life stage. Through self-assessment questionnaires, interactive group discussions, and guided reflections (involv-ing spouses where relevant), participants are empowered to design a personalised transition plan that balances profes-sional closure, emotional well-being, and future aspirations. This initiative ensures that every leader feels valued, support-ed, and connected to our purpose, even as they step into a new chapter of life.

Attendance and discipline indicators such as improved employee attendance (up to 50% improvement), reduction in absenteeism, and fewer disciplinary cases. Human Rights 
At ABFRL, respect for human rights is a foundational prin-
ciple that guides how we operate and engage across the organisation. We are committed to fostering a workplace where every individual is treated with dignity, fairness, and respect, and where equal opportunity is consistently upheld at every level.
Our Board approved Human Rights Policy, aligned with 
the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, es-tablishes a clear and robust framework for our commitments. It reinforces our uncompromising stance against discrimina-tion, harassment, and any form of unfair treatment, extend-ing across our employees, workers, and value chain partners.
These principles are embedded into our day-to-day 
operations through a comprehensive governance framework anchored in our Code of Conduct and supporting policies. From recruitment and development to performance man-agement and workplace interactions, we integrate these standards across the employee lifecycle, ensuring consisten-cy, accountability, and alignment with our commitment to uphold human rights.
Our approach is supported by structured monitoring 
and grievance redressal mechanisms that enable employees to raise concerns in a confidential, fair, and timely manner. During the reporting year, we further strengthened these systems to enhance effectiveness and transparency. We introduced a Values Governance and Consequence Man-agement Toolkit, enabling a consistent and fair approach to handling values-related matters across business units. This was complemented by the implementation of a standardised operating procedure (SOP) covering the reporting, investiga-tion, and closure of cases, ensuring uniformity and clarity in processes.
We also established a structured consequence manage-
ment framework, aligning actions with the nature and sever-ity of cases, while balancing corrective and disciplinary mea-sures. In addition, improvements were made to case tracking, documentation, and periodic review mechanisms, enabling better oversight, accountability, and timely resolution.
These enhancements reflect our commitment to strength-
ening trust and ensuring that every concern is addressed with integrity and sensitivity. During the reporting year, there were no human rights-related complaints or cases reported, reflecting the effectiveness of our policies and practices.
Through these sustained efforts, we continue to reinforce 
a culture where respect for human rights is not only a policy requirement but a lived organisational value.
Human Rights Commitment
At ABFRL, human rights extend beyond compliance. They represent our commitment to fostering an environment defined by safety, respect, and fairness for every individual across our ecosystem.
We adopt a proactive approach to safeguarding hu-
man rights by strictly prohibiting practices such as modern slavery, child labour, forced or involuntary labour, human trafficking, and all forms of harassment. We maintain a zero-tolerance stance on discrimination and are committed to ensuring equitable treatment irrespective of race, caste, religion, colour, gender, sexual orientation, age, nationality, ethnic origin, disability, or any other legally protected charac-teristic.
This uncompromising approach is embedded across our 
operations and upheld through robust governance frame-works. We are also committed to protecting vulnerable and under-represented groups, including women, migrant workers, minorities, and indigenous communities. During FY 2025–26, there were no reported incidents involving indige-nous communities, reflecting our strong preventive focus.
Additionally, we uphold fair working conditions and 
equitable remuneration practices through regular monitoring of working hours, adherence to overtime norms, and ongoing engagement with employee and worker representatives to ensure safe, compliant, and inclusive workplaces across all locations.
Respect for individual rights is further reflected in our support for the freedom of association. We uphold every employee’s right to freely form or join trade unions without fear of retaliation. Currently, none of our workforce is covered under collective bargaining agreements, and we ensure that employees are provided with a minimum of 60 days’ notice for any significant operational changes, in alignment with union agreements.

Human Rights Risk Management
At ABFRL, we recognise that safeguarding human rights requires more than intent it demands proactive systems, vigi-lant oversight, and continuous risk assessment. Our approach focuses on anticipating potential risks early and embedding preventive measures across our operations and value chain.
Through our Human Rights Due Diligence Framework, 
we undertake comprehensive and systematic risk mapping prior to entering any new partnerships, mergers and ac-quisitions, or joint ventures. This enables us to identify and mitigate potential human rights concerns at the outset. 
We follow a proactive approach to human rights risk 
management across our operations and value chain. During FY 2025–26, we conducted extensive assessments across our operations and supplier ecosystem, covering key areas such as child labour, forced labour, sexual harassment, discrimi-nation, human trafficking, freedom of association, equal pay, and wage compliance. These assessments extended across Tier 1 vendors, warehouses, retail stores, corporate offices, and in-house manufacturing facilities. While, no significant risks were identified during the reporting period, we main-tain preventive mitigation action plans across 100% of our operational sites and key suppliers through established policies, due diligence processes and ongoing monitoring mechanisms.
To further reinforce our preventive framework, we intro-
duced targeted initiatives aimed at strengthening control and transparency. These included the implementation of Aad-haar-based age verification systems across manufacturing sites to mitigate child labour risks, expansion of anonymous feedback channels to enable safe and confidential reporting of workplace concerns and enhanced inclusive hiring proto-cols to minimise potential bias and discrimination. In addi-tion, we strengthened our contractor management processes through more robust onboarding documentation and clearly defined safety and compliance expectations, ensuring ethical labour practices across contract workforces.
Through these structured and forward-looking mea-
sures, we aim to ensure that human rights risk management remains embedded, proactive, and integral to our operational excellence.

our structured training programmes. During FY 2025–26, we delivered 5,819 hours of dedicated human rights train-ing through e-learning platforms across corporate, retail,

Grievance Redressal 
We have established a transparent, accessible, and robust 
grievance redressal system that ensures every issue is ad-dressed with fairness, confidentiality, and accountability.
We have also institutionalised robust mechanisms to en-
sure a safe and respectful workplace. An Internal Complaints Committee, constituted in line with the POSH Act, is respon-sible for the timely and effective handling of complaints. Em-ployees have access to multiple reporting channels, including a toll-free hotline, enabling them to raise concerns directly with the ABFRL Value Committee, HR, or their managers with confidence. Additionally, all our employees are provided with training on the use of these reporting channels, in line with our whistleblowing policy.
Our grievance framework is anchored in a fully digital, 
end-to-end complaint management system, enabling the efficient handling of Code of Conduct violations and Preven-tion of Sexual Harassment (POSH) cases. Each business unit is supported by dedicated and trained committees for both Values-related matters and POSH, with the latter comprising an external member in accordance with statutory require-ments. These committees conduct thorough and unbiased investigations, ensuring that every complaint undergoes appropriate scrutiny prior to resolution.
Our broader governance framework is supported by 
multiple policies and mechanisms that reinforce ethical con-duct and safe reporting. These include our Anti-Fraud Policy, Vigil Mechanism, and Whistleblower Policy, which provide secure and accessible channels for employees, partners, and vendors to report concerns or potential violations. The integrated Complaint Management System (CMS) enables re-al-time tracking, case categorisation, and analytical insights, enhancing transparency, responsiveness, and oversight.
All grievances are routed through Integrity Matters, our 
third-party managed platform, which allows reporting via multiple channels, including email, telephone, website, and postal communication. This ensures both accessibility and strict confidentiality, while enabling complete traceability of each case. To maintain consistency and control, complaints are not accepted through informal or offline channels. De-fined timelines are adhered to, with resolution of Values-re-lated cases within 30 days and POSH cases within 90 days, aligned with regulatory norms.
During FY 2025–26, 119 complaints related to values 
violations were reported, with 13 cases pending resolution at the end of the reporting period. Zero case of workplace discrimination was reported. These disclosures reflect a culture of openness and trust, where individuals feel confi-dent in raising concerns, secure in the knowledge that their voices will be heard and addressed without fear of adverse consequences.

At ABFRL, safety is a fundamental pillar of our operational 
excellence and a key enabler of sustainable growth. An-chored in our sustainability programme, ReEarth – For Our Tomorrow, we are committed to fostering a safe, secure, and resilient work environment that supports employee wellbeing while strengthening engagement and retention.
Safety Governance
We are cognizant that a workplace that is safe and sound is essential to attract talented and engaged employees. To ensure safety, we have a dedicated Business Review Council (BRC) at the board level that oversees the overall imple-mentation of our safety policies and reviews its performance quarterly. Our three-tier approach to safety performance includes an initial review by the site safety committee fol-lowed by the business safety committee/sub-committee and finally by the Business Review Council. The CSO monitors OHS performance and communicates with the Management Committee and RMSC. Further, the RMSC provides oversight on safety-related matters and strategies. 
Safety governance is reinforced through site-level com-
mittees comprising equal representation from management and employees, fostering collaboration and shared owner-ship. Workers actively contribute to risk assessments and improvement initiatives, while regular meetings are held to review performance, address risks, and drive accountability. 
A structured incident reporting and investigation frame-
work ensures that all incidents and near misses are promptly reported, recorded, and addressed. Incidents are escalated to the relevant area in-charge, safety officer, HR manager, and facility manager, in line with the defined reporting matrix communicated across the organisation. All events are logged through the ReEarth Sustainability Portal, with designated personnel responsible for timely reporting based on incident severity.
Worker Participation and Consultation
We actively promote meaningful worker participation and consultation across all stages of our OHS Management System, including its development, implementation, and evaluation. This is enabled through structured mechanisms that encourage engagement, ownership, and continuous feedback.
A formal Joint Safety Committee is established across all 
manufacturing and warehouse facilities, with equal represen-tation from management and workers. Worker representa-tives are elected at regular intervals, ensuring fair representa-tion and active participation. The committee meets monthly at manufacturing facilities, sampling units and warehouses to review OHS performance, discuss hazards, and drive continu-ous improvement.
In addition, our Safety Observation Programme fosters 
proactive engagement between supervisors, line managers, and workers on the shop floor. Observations on safe and unsafe behaviours and conditions are systematically record-ed and analysed, with insights fed into the HIRA process and corrective action plans.
We also provide multiple channels for hazard and near-
miss reporting, including direct reporting to supervisors, safety registers, and digital platforms. All reported con-cerns are acknowledged, investigated, and addressed, with feedback provided to the reporting individual, reinforcing transparency and trust.
Managers and line leaders actively engage with workers 
to identify risks and encourage open reporting of safety concerns. Site-level safety committees promote employee participation and shared responsibility in maintaining safe workplaces.
Our Approach to Occupational Health  
and Safety
During FY 2025–26, we strengthened our Occupational 
Health and Safety (OHS) framework to ensure comprehen-sive coverage across all operational sites, aligned with appli-cable legal and regulatory requirements. Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) have been systematically implemented across manufacturing facilities, sampling units, warehouses, and retail locations, driving consistency and discipline in safety practices across the organisation. 
Our approach is anchored in continuous risk assessment, 
proactive mitigation, and ongoing performance improve-ment. This has delivered tangible outcomes, including zero workplace fatalities during the year, reflecting the robustness of our systems and the strong commitment of our workforce.
Routine safety inspections are conducted at defined 
intervals across shop floor and facility levels, using stan-dardised checklists covering equipment, housekeeping, Per-HUMAN CAPITAL
=== page 63 ===
76

sonal Protective Equipment (PPE) compliance, and safe work 
practices. Annual internal audits, undertaken by qualified and cross-functional teams, assess the overall effectiveness of the OHS management system, with findings categorised by risk severity- high, medium, or low to enable prioritised action. Key observations, particularly high-risk issues, are escalated to senior leadership through established governance mecha-nisms, ensuring timely decision-making and effective closure.
Following any incident, an investigation team is consti-
tuted to conduct root cause analysis, with corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) implemented within defined timelines to prevent recurrence. This process is supported by digital tools, including QR-based reporting systems, which enable employees to easily raise safety concerns and enhance reporting transparency.
To strengthen prevention and mitigation, we enhanced 
the reporting and monitoring of safety observations and near-miss incidents through our digital EHS systems. Guided by the Heinrich Safety Triangle principle, we adopted a pro-active approach focused on early identification and resolu-tion of risks before they escalate into Lost Time Injuries (LTIs) or serious incidents.
We conducted regular internal and external safety audits, 
inspections, and compliance assessments to identify gaps and implement CAPA. Structured risk registers were main-tained to track critical risks and infrastructure improvements, with high-priority observations reviewed through manage-ment governance forums to ensure timely closure.
To further strengthen operational control, high-risk and 
non-routine activities are governed by a structured Work Permit System, ensuring appropriate safeguards are in place before work begins. The Lockout–Tagout (LOTO) system is rigorously implemented to control hazardous energy, sup-ported by engineering controls. In addition, clear Operating Control Procedures (OCPs), regular training, and a well-de-fined PPE matrix ensure the safe execution of tasks across all functions.Periodic self-assessments are also conducted to evaluate 
preparedness in critical areas such as fire safety and emer-gency response, reinforcing our commitment to continuous improvement and operational resilience.
This framework is further strengthened through exter-
nal audits conducted at selected facilities by independent third-party bodies, providing objective validation of compli-ance and implementation effectiveness. 
Safety is embedded across the entire lifecycle of our op-
erations, including new projects, expansions, modifications, and acquisitions. Each initiative undergoes comprehensive risk assessment followed by structured mitigation planning. A robust change management process ensures that emerg-ing risks are proactively identified and addressed, while an inherently safer design approach minimises risks at source. 
Safety Management System
Our OHS Management System is aligned with the ABG Tech-nical Standard, designed to enable a Zero Harm environment. It encompasses eight core elements: leadership commitment; policy and strategic objectives; organisation, resources and competence; risk evaluation and management; planning, standards and procedures; implementation, monitoring and reporting; inspection and assurance; and management review. These elements are supported by detailed sub-com-ponents to ensure rigour, consistency, and accountability at every level. All our operational sites, employees and workers are fully covered by an occupational health and safety man-agement system that complies with legal requirements and recognised standards.
Risk Assessment and Monitoring
Our Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) process provides a comprehensive framework for evaluating risks across physical, electrical, fire, chemical, ergonomic, and psychosocial domains. Identified hazards are assessed based on their level of significance, and appropriate control mea-sures are implemented in line with the hierarchy of controls, including elimination, substitution, engineering controls, administrative controls, and the use of PPE.
HIRA is reviewed periodically, following incidents, and 
prior to the introduction of new activities, ensuring its ongo-ing relevance and effectiveness. Insights from near-miss and incident investigations are systematically fed back into the process to drive continuous improvement.
This internal framework is further strengthened through 
external assessments at selected sites, validating alignment with applicable OHS standards. In addition, a dedicated mon-itoring application tracks critical parameters such as tempera-ture, pressure, and fire system performance, enabling real-time alerts and timely interventions to proactively manage risks. 
To enhance preventive controls and emergency pre-
paredness, we also implemented an IoT-based Real-Time Safety Equipment Monitoring System (RSEMS) at select critical locations, including Jaypore/S&N Warehouse (Noida), Shantnu & Nikhil Head Office (Noida), and Pantaloons distri-bution centres across regions. This system enables real-time monitoring of critical infrastructure such as fire pumps, alarm systems, UPS room conditions, and fire water tanks ensur-ing operational readiness, early detection of anomalies, and timely intervention.
During the reporting year, a third-party agency conduct-
ed safety audits across key locations. This includes safety au-dits at 49 stores and four warehouses to ensure compliance with safety standards. Additionally, fire and electrical safety audit was conducted at TCNS facility- office, warehouse and sampling unit.

To complement our risk management approach, we track OHS performance through a robust MIS-driven framework that includes both lagging and leading indicators, monitored monthly across all facilities.

Accelerating Circularity in Fashion   
At ABFRL, sustainability and circularity are embedded across the product lifecycle—from design and material selection to manufacturing, consumer use and end-of-life management. We prioritise durable design, responsible sourcing and re-source-efficient production to extend garment lifecycles and reduce waste. The use of lower-impact materials, including BCI cotton, recycled polyester and biodegradable fibres, helps minimise our environmental footprint.
Our clothing take-back programme and recycling part-
nerships support the reuse and repurposing of textiles, while brands across our portfolio are advancing circularity through innovative initiatives. Jaypore upcycles sarees into contem-porary apparel, and Shantnu & Nikhil’s Buy Back Programme encourages customers to return used garments for store credit. Recognised by the Ellen MacArthur Foundation’s Circular Design for Fashion programme, our approach is supported by clear governance, accountability and ongoing efforts to strengthen circular economy practices and create long-term value.
We also actively collaborate with national and global 
industry platforms and organisations, including RECEIC, BIS, Textile Exchange, ICC, WBCSD, and ESG Task Forces, to con-tribute to industry-wide sustainability priorities, share best practices, and advance responsible and sustainable business practices.
Accelerating Circularity in Indian Textiles: 
Aditya Birla Fashion–GIZ develoPPP Project 
To advance circularity in the Indian textile and apparel sector, 
Aditya Birla Fashion partnered with GIZ Germany under the three-year develoPPP programme. Launched in 2021, the Approaches for Circular Textiles and Apparel Industry in India (ACT) project promotes circular practices through innovation, capacity building and collaboration across the value chain. Implemented with the Centre for Environment Education (CEE) and supported by the International Council for Circular Economy (ICCE) as knowledge partner, the initiative brings together industry and development expertise to drive sec-tor-wide change.
Guided by a multi-stakeholder Steering Committee, the 
project focuses on strengthening industry capacity to adopt circular business practices. Key areas include reducing harm-ful inputs, advancing textile recycling, extending product lifecycles through reuse, and promoting alternative materials and renewable energy. Contributing to SDGs 5, 8, 10, 12, 13 and 17, the initiative supports a more inclusive, resource-effi-cient and low-waste textile value chain.
Key Components & Milestones 
CIRCULARITY BASELINE ASSESSMENT To build a clearer view of circularity across the textile indus-try, a pan-India assessment was carried out to map key chal-lenges, identify high impact areas, and define intervention priorities. The survey brought together perspectives from more than 90 stakeholders, spanning textile mills, garment-ing units, processing and dyeing units, waste processing agencies, brands, retail stores, consumers, government minis-tries and associations, as well as academic institutions. The insights from this comprehensive assessment were officially launched at the International Circular Economy Forum (ICEF) held in New Delhi. 
Innovation Challenge 
An innovation challenge was conducted on GIZ leverist plat-form to identify scalable circularity solutions. The initiative received 87 submissions, out of which 9 were shortlisted for industry adoption following evaluation by an external jury. All innovations were compiled into a booklet that was officially launched at Bharat Tex in the presence of the Joint Secretary and senior representatives from Aditya Birla Fashion and GIZ.
Demonstration Project 
We identified three circularity projects from the innovation challenge and successfully implemented in brands. While the remaining projects were made available for adoption by other industry stakeholders.
Capacity Building on Circularity 
A comprehensive training curriculum was developed, con-sisting of three tailored modules for the leadership team, middle management, and trainers. The programme was rolled out across nine key textile clusters in India, reaching 426 participants from diverse stakeholder groups. As part of the initiative, a two day Training of Trainers (ToT) programme was conducted, covering Circular Fashion, Advanced Waste Management, Circular Business Models, and Innovative Circu-lar Strategies. This initiative resulted in the creation of a pool of 26 certified trainers from senior and middle management levels.
Development of Guidelines 
The ‘Stitching the Circle’ Circularity Guidelines and Manifesto were developed through an extensive stakeholder engage-ment process, including seven focus group consultations across textile clusters in India and the broader textile value chain. The process brought together over 300 stakeholders, along with a dedicated 24-member working group repre-senting brands, academia, recyclers, textile mills, NGOs, and innovators. Guided by three key priorities: strong stakeholder engagement, key performance metrics for benchmarking, and dissemination to industry and government- the draft was refined through multiple consultations and finalised by the working group. The guidelines were officially released at the Sankalp Summit and Bharat Tex, marking an important step in advancing circularity across the industry. The guideline establishes circular economy practices clearly and offers a structured pathway to reduce dependency on virgin resourc-es and promote waste-to-value initiatives.Communications 
The Aditya Birla Fashion-GIZ collaboration gained strong vis-ibility through coverage across leading media outlets, indus-try conferences, global forums, and social media platforms. The Circular Business Guidelines were disseminated with over 5,000 stakeholders within the Indian textile sector, fostering broader industry awareness and engagement on circularity.
Driving Alignment through Knowledge  
and Advocacy 
An industry working group was formulated to strengthen 
alignment and collaboration across stakeholders. We carried out a detailed mapping of global policies, which led to the development of a policy white paper aimed to support circu-larity efforts in the Indian textile sector. In addition, advocacy efforts continued through participation in industry forums and active engagement with government bodies to support broader systemic change.

It outlines measures for continuous improvement of security systems, ensuring integrity and data protection, and monitoring and responding to evolving risks. Personal data, encryption keys, and other sensitive information are handled only after appropriate legal and privacy evaluations. In the event of any breach, we take appropriate disciplinary action depending on the nature of violation.
Information security governance is organised such that

Information Security Controls 
Our IT systems and infrastructure are aligned with the ISO 27001 Information Security Management System standard and the NIST 853 framework, reflecting our strong focus on protecting information assets. During the previous year, we upgraded our certification to ISO 27001:2022. To uphold these standards, we carry out regular internal audits of our IT systems and infrastructure, along with reviews to ensure compliance with our Information Security Policy. These assessments help ensure consistent adherence and maintain system integrity across the organisation. We also undertake independent external audits aligned with ISO 27001 to vali-date both technical controls and policy implementation.
During the year, we enhanced our cybersecurity posture 
by strengthening protection and monitoring across critical layers of our IT environment. We have upgraded our End-point security from traditional antivirus systems to next gen-eration Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), enabling real time detection and response to cyber threats. Security of public facing websites has been reinforced through advanced controls, including DNS security measures to block malicious communications and prevent ransomware attacks, along with the deployment of Cloud Web Application Firewall (WAF) solutions to safeguard e commerce and other internet facing platforms.
Our cloud security capabilities have also been enhanced 
by improving visibility and risk management across AWS workloads, identities, and configurations. In parallel, identity protection has been strengthened through the implemen-tation of next generation Privileged Access Management solutions, along with multi factor authentication controls for internal users and third party contractors, ensuring tighter control over access across the ecosystem.
Our security approach follows a defense in depth model, 
supported by multiple layers of controls. These include safeguards covering physical infrastructure, networks, identities, access controls, applications, endpoints, and data. All controls are continuously monitored through Security Incident and Event Management (SIEM) systems, managed by our dedicated security operations team. We also sub-scribe to cyber threat intelligence services that provide alerts on potential threats, enabling timely patching and preventive actions to mitigate risks.
We conduct annual vulnerability assessments and 
penetration testing using both internal teams and external experts. Additionally, we undertake red teaming exercises that simulate real life attack scenarios to identify hidden vulnerabilities. These exercises assess the preparedness of our people, systems, and processes. The findings provide actionable insights to strengthen our security framework and enhance resilience against cyber threats and data breaches.

We strongly emphasise on cybersecurity and data privacy 
through continuous training and awareness programmes for our employees and third party contractors. Our flagship initiative, Cyber Jagruti, delivers mandatory sessions cov-ering IT security controls, prevention of data breaches, and responsible handling of Personally Identifiable Information (PII). The programme includes periodic LMS-based training modules for new joiners as well as existing employees, while annual refresher trainings ensure that knowledge remains up-to-date. 
To keep our workforce informed and vigilant, we use a 
variety of training formats such as emailers, videos, presen-tations, and course materials, along with phishing simulations to assess awareness and compliance with policies. A dedicat-ed Cyber Jagruti channel on Teams helps us keep the staff updated on evolving data security and privacy protocols. We also share cybersecurity mailers that highlight safe practices for both company and personal systems.
Business Continuity 
Ensuring operational resilience remains a key priority for us, and we have established a robust business continuity plan (BCP) to protect our operations. Our cloud based disaster recovery site acts as a safeguard to ensure continuity during unforeseen disruptions. In addition, we have put in place a Cyber Incident Response and Recovery process to minimise interruptions arising from cybersecurity incidents. 
We have strengthened the reliability of our IT environ-
ment with a focus on high availability for critical infrastruc-ture and security systems. Applications are deployed across multiple zones, regions, and data centres, supported by SaaS based offerings, regular backups with offsite storage, and ongoing monitoring and capacity planning. Our systems are designed to scale both horizontally and vertically, while a tiered security approach ensures appropriate levels of pro-tection across the ecosystem. Our IT processes align with ITIL based standards, and systems are regularly reviewed through ITGC and ISO 27001 audits to validate reliability and support continuity of critical business operations. Regular main-tenance, updates, and periodic testing of our BCP ensure ongoing preparedness and effectiveness.
Regular maintenance, updates, and semiannual testing of 
our business continuity plans are conducted to validate their effectiveness and ensure readiness to respond to contin-gencies. These proactive efforts strengthen our operational resilience and help reduce the impact of potential disruptions on our business operations.
Customer Data privacy 
Our approach to data privacy is supported by robust mea-sures, including data leakage prevention systems, encryption of data in transit using Transport Layer Security (TLS), strong access controls, and multifactor authentication protocols. These controls are supported by ongoing enhancement of our systems. Through these efforts, we aim to ensure the confidentiality and integrity of customer data, protecting it from unauthorised access or misuse.
In line with our privacy policy, customers have the right 
to request deletion or correction of their personal data by contacting the grievance officer via email. In compliance with GDPR and CCPA requirements, international users visit-ing our brand websites are presented with a cookie consent pop up, allowing them to choose whether to opt in or opt out of data tracking.
Incident Response Mechanism 
Aligned with Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) standards, we have established a robust and well defined incident management framework. Any indication of suspicious activity or potential security breach is reported through our helpdesk portal and promptly escalated to the appropriate stakeholders, ensuring timely response and resolution within defined Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
Our escalation framework enables employees to report 
incidents, vulnerabilities, or suspicious activities swiftly and effectively. This streamlined approach ensures that poten-tial risks are identified, and addressed at the earliest stage, fostering a proactive and alert security culture across the organisation. Employees are supported by an internal tick-eting system for efficient reporting. Dedicated and trained personnel oversee the investigation of information secu-rity incidents and carry out detailed root cause analyses to identify underlying issues and prevent recurrence. The findings are reviewed by respective business unit IT teams, while critical findings with wider implications are escalated for approval by the Chief Digital and Information Technolo-gy Officer.
Over the past three financial years, no instances of data 
breaches or information security lapses have been report-ed. We have received no substantiated complaints from stakeholders regarding data breaches, including concerns related to customer privacy, further reflecting our continued commitment to protecting data and maintaining stakeholder trust.

ESG Governance
Our ESG governance framework follows a structured, multi-layered approach that ensures robust oversight of ESG and climate-related risks while promoting transparency and ethical decision making.
At the highest level, the Board of Directors provides 
strategic oversight by approving sustainability policies and guiding senior management on ESG initiatives. Semi-annual Board meetings focus on climate-related risks and opportu-nities, strategies, policies, and overall performance to ensure alignment with long-term sustainability objectives. The Board-level Risk Management and Sustainability Committee (RMSC) plays a key role in monitoring and addressing ESG matters, including climate-related issues. Meeting bi-annually, the Committee reviews progress and reports updates to the Board. In addition, the Board of Directors, including RMSC members, regularly participates in capacity-building sessions on emerging ESG developments.
Leadership engagement is central to advancing our sus-
tainability agenda. The Managing Director defines the overall strategic direction, while the Chief Sustainability Officer (CSO) leads the development and execution of sustainability and climate strategies. The CSO conducts quarterly reviews to monitor progress in implementing CSR and sustainabili-ty initiatives. Budget allocations for CSR and sustainability programs are strategically planned and approved to ensure alignment with business objectives, with oversight and guid-ance from the Board-level Risk Management and Sustainabil-ity Committee (RMSC) and the Corporate Social Responsibili-ty Committee (CSRC).
Furthermore, a Management Committee consisting of 
CXOs and senior management enabling has been set up to ensure effective communication and cooperation across departments, leading to the seamless integration of ESG principles into business operations. At the operational level, implementation teams conduct bi-monthly discussions with business unit heads to address sustainability and climate-re-lated concerns across factories, warehouses, and retail outlets. These regular interactions ensure that employees remain actively involved and empowered to contribute to sustainability initiatives, strengthening a culture of responsi-bility across the organisation. 
Financial incentives play a pivotal role in driving sustain-
ability performance and ensuring alignment with climate and sustainability targets. ESG KPIs are integrated into the vari-
able remuneration of the Management Committee, including CEOs, the CSO, and other CXOs. These performance-linked incentives extend to functional heads and sustainability team members.
 
Climate Strategy
 
At ABFRL, we recognise the industry’s influence on climate change, and actively work to mitigate the environmental im-pact of our operations and products. Climate considerations are integral to financial, strategic, and operational decisions, ensuring a responsible approach to sustainability. 
Our near-term emission reduction targets, validated 
by the Science Based Targets Initiative (SBTi), reflect an unwavering commitment to climate action. We are targeting a 54.6% absolute reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions by FY 2032-33 against the FY 2022-23 baseline, alongside a 32.5% absolute reduction in Scope 3 emissions across purchased goods and services, fuel and energy-related activities, and franchises within the same timeframe. We are also aligned with the Aditya Birla Group’s decarbonisation strategy, pursuing net zero carbon emissions by 2050 through energy efficiency programmes, low carbon growth, product stew-ardship, and carbon sequestration projects. Periodic climate change risk assessments are conducted in accordance with the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) to evaluate climate-related challenges across all operational sites including existing manufacturing facilities, warehouses, and retail stores, as well as upstream and down-stream activities.
Climate risks are assessed against current and anticipat-ed regulations, technological shifts, legal exposure, market dynamics, reputational considerations, and both acute and chronic physical risks. These risks and opportunities are fur-ther incorporated into the company’s centralised enterprise risk management framework. Risk evaluation spans three distinct timeframes: short-term (up to 2030), medium-term (2030–2040), and long-term (beyond 2040). Scenario analyses leverage the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Representation Concentration Pathways (RCP 2.6, RCP 4.5, RCP 6, and RCP 8.5) and Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-1.9, SSP1- 2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, SSP5-8.5) to assess potential physical risks, including temperature and precipitation fluctuations across operational sites. Addition-ally, transition risks are analysed using scenarios from the International Energy Agency (IEA), including the Net Zero Emissions by 2050 Scenario (NZE), the Announced Pledges Scenario (APS), the Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS), and the Sustainable Development Scenario (SDS). These insights, derived from both quantitative and qualitative models, help identify climate risks, develop mitigation strategies, and cap-italise on emerging opportunities. To build resilience against identified risks, comprehensive, context-specific plans have been developed covering 100% of operations including all new facilities, with adaptation measures prioritised for implementation within five years, ensuring the organisation remains agile and well-prepared to navigate climate-related challenges.
We have established a transition plan to align with global 
net-zero GHG emission goals, with a clear commitment to supporting the Paris Agreement objective of limiting global warming to 1.5°C. Our approach includes defined decarboni-sation levers and planned actions to drive progress towards our emission reduction targets. We actively engage with key stakeholders, including our value chain partners and indus-try associations, to gather inputs and support the effective implementation of our transition pathway. Through these efforts, we aim to progressively advance our climate strategy and strengthen alignment with global climate commitments.
During 2025, Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited 
(ABFRL) underwent organisational restructuring through the demerger of its business operations, resulting in formation of two independently listed entities: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Limited (ABFRL) and Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL). 
As ABFRL’s near-term science-based emissions reduction

targets were validated by the Science Based Targets initia-
tive (SBTi) in 2024, the demerger necessitated a review of the Company’s greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory and target applicability in accordance with the SBTi Corporate Net-Zero and Near-Term Criteria.
Consistent with SBTi requirements, ABFRL sought formal 
guidance on the implications of the demerger for its validat-ed targets and base year emissions inventory. SBTi guid-ance specifies that companies must recalculate their base year emissions where structural changes, such as mergers, acquisitions, divestments, or demergers; result in a material change to the emissions inventory. Such recalculations are intended to preserve consistency, transparency, and compa-rability of progress against established targets.
SBTi further clarified that a recalculation of base year 
emissions does not automatically trigger target revalidation. Existing validated targets may continue to remain valid, provided that the recalculated inventory does not materially alter the ambition level, organisational boundary, target cov-erage, or methodological alignment of the original commit-ment. Revalidation is generally required only where structural change significantly affects the integrity or ambition of the approved target pathway.
Accordingly, ABFRL undertook a detailed assessment 
internally, to evaluate the impact of the demerger on its sci-ence-based targets. The assessment concluded that although the demerger constitutes a material structural change requir-ing recalculation of base year emissions, it does not affect the underlying ambition, target methodology, or coverage requirements of the existing SBTi-approved targets.
Following the recalculation exercise, both ABFRL and 
ABLBL continue to satisfy the minimum target-boundary coverage thresholds prescribed by SBTi:

As both entities continue to meet the applicable SBTi

ENERGY CONSERVATION INITIATIVES
Energy Efficiency at PantaloonsThe energy efficiency project at Pantaloons retail stores leveraged IoT technology to optimise HVAC energy con-sumption, enhancing sustainability and reducing costs. Pilot stores were selected, two in Bangalore and two in Chennai, for implementation and monitoring. Between May and June 2024, IoT-based HVAC optimisation was deployed, enabling real-time data analysis and precise energy control. Results showed significant energy savings: Chennai’s Keelambakam store saved 145.7 kWh daily, Pallavakam 71.4 kWh, Ban-galore’s Niladri 91.2 kWh, and Kammanahalli 26 kWh. The project delivered a 20% cost reduction in three months, saving ₹1,17,356 per month, with 100% ROI achieved in seven months. This initiative highlights the impact of technolo-gy driven optimisation in retail sustainability. Its success provides a strong foundation for scaling energy efficiency measures across more locations, reinforcing our commitment to responsible operations.
TCNS warehouse PV SRT
A 274 kWp rooftop solar photovoltaic system is installed at the TCNS warehouse. During the reporting period, the site consumed 58,296 kWh of renewable electricity from the solar installation, contributing to its renewable energy consumption.

Water Discharge
We manage water discharge efficiently, ensuring minimal environmental impact while maintaining responsible water stewardship. Since our operations focus solely on retailing and warehousing hence do not involve fabric production, the wastewater we generate consists only of domestic sewage. 
Water discharge takes place through municipal lines and 
onsite sewage treatment plants (STPs), ensuring appropriate treatment across our facilities. Treated water is reused for gardening and flushing purposes. Water quality is rigorously monitored in compliance with state pollution control guide-lines, with adherence maintained across all national, regional, and local air and water consent requirements. Regular testing of physical, chemical, and biological parameters ensures full compliance before any wastewater is discharged into municipal sewers. These initiatives help us minimise fresh-water withdrawals, mitigate pollution risks, and reinforce our commitment to sustainable water management.

To reduce freshwater dependency in these areas, we deploy enhanced recycling systems, rainwater harvesting infrastructure, and water-efficient technologies, reinforcing our commitment to responsible water management and sustainability

Waste Management  
We recognise that strategic waste management is integral to reducing environmental impact, conserving natural resourc-es, and strengthening operational sustainability. We have established clear guidelines and Standard Operating Proce-dures (SOPs) across waste streams to ensure proper segre-gation, handling, and disposal, enabling safe and sustainable waste management practices across our operations.
Our waste-related impacts primarily arise from materi-
al
-
intensive inputs such as textiles, chemicals, and packaging. 
Our manufacturing and retail operations generate significant pre-consumer waste, including fabric scraps and packag-ing, as well as hazardous waste streams such as used oil, oil-soaked cotton, batteries, e-waste, and biomedical waste. These wastes, generated from activities including DG set operations, equipment maintenance, and IT infrastructure usage, present environmental risks such as landfill burden, resource loss, and potential pollution, requiring specialised handling and disposal.
While the most direct impacts originate from our own 
operations, we also recognise upstream impacts from vendor manufacturing processes and downstream impacts related to post-consumer textile and packaging waste. We actively work across our value chain to mitigate these impacts by promoting circular practices, sustainable material use, opti-mised packaging, and responsible disposal through autho-rised recyclers.
We maintain a robust waste governance framework 
involving authorised third-party vendors for collection and disposal. Vendors are selected through stringent due diligence based on credibility, regulatory authorisation, and compliance, with approvals obtained from relevant func-tions including Legal and Supply Chain. Waste traceability is ensured through a three-step data management approach involving manual logbooks at facilities, vendor confirmation and receipts, and centralised reporting through a digital sus-tainability management portal, supporting third-party audit and assurance.
Our approach follows a lifecycle-based model focused 
on waste prevention through efficient material use, process optimisation, and digitalisation to reduce both hazardous and paper waste. We emphasise segregation at source, safe handling, and maximising recycling and reuse, with minimal reliance on landfill disposal. 
We conduct regular training and awareness programmes for employees to promote responsible waste management practices, including segregation, handling, and regulatory compliance. Periodic waste audits are undertaken to assess waste generation patterns, evaluate segregation efficiency, and identify improvement opportunities, with findings trans-lated into targeted action plans.
We have ambition to achieve zero waste to landfill with 
100% traceability across all owned facilities by 2030, with a focus on progressively minimising waste generation. Invest-ments in innovative technologies, including automated cut-ting and marking tools, have significantly optimised material usage and reduced fabric waste. These efforts, supported by continuous employee engagement, reinforce our commit-ment to circularity and long-term sustainability.
We aim to establish end-to-end waste traceability, sup-
ported by regular audits and ongoing monitoring of disposal systems, enabling us to validate safe handling practices, accurately track waste volumes directed to authorised recy-clers, and identify performance improvement opportunities. Biomedical and sanitary waste undergo incineration, ensur-ing safe treatment, while non-hazardous waste is either recy-cled or repurposed. Food waste is composted using in-house vermicompost, converting it into bio-manure for agricultural use. All disposal processes comply with applicable regula-tory requirements, and disposal facilities and recyclers are selected through a thorough due diligence process, ensuring no contamination during disposal.

Packaging Management 
We continuously strive to strengthen our systems and processes and, as a leader in the apparel retail sector, have committed to using 100% sustainable packaging material by 2030. Our packaging strategy considers packaging com-ponents and focuses on design optimisation, reduction and recycling. During the period from November 2025 to March 31, 2026, the Jaypore warehouse implemented a carton shredding initiative that enabled the reuse of approximately 4.95 MT of discarded cartons by converting them into honeycomb protective packaging material. This intervention significantly reduced the reliance on conventional plastic-based packag-ing materials, bringing down total packaging consumption from ~575 kg/month to ~140kg/month. As a result,  ~434kg of packaging material was avoided each month, amounting to ~2MT over the five-month period. Overall, the initiative demonstrates a strong circular economy approach by elim-inating high-impact materials such as thermocol and foam sheets, optimising resource efficiency, and delivering measur -
able environmental benefits.
Raw Material Management 
Responsible sourcing of raw materials is fundamental to 
minimising environmental impact and sustaining ethical sup-ply chains within the apparel retail sector. At ABFRL, we are committed to scaling the use of sustainable materials while maintaining the highest standards of social responsibility and environmental stewardship.
We have developed an internal framework for sustain-
able attributes that encompasses sustainable raw materials, production processes, manufacturing facilities, packaging, and sustainable livelihoods. A consolidated target has been established for the proportion of sustainable and recycled raw materials, with performance monitored and reported on both a half-yearly and annual basis. In FY 2025-26, 95% of our products had at least one sustainable attribute. By 2030, we aim to incorporate at least one sustainable attribute across 100% of our garments, by volume. 
As part of this commitment, we source high-quality raw 
materials with a focus on minimising environmental and social impacts across the value chain. Guided by recognised tools and standards, we prioritise the use of responsibly sourced and lower-impact materials, including BCI Cotton, Liva Eco, FSC-certified Birla Modal, and recycled fibres, while maintaining high standards of quality, performance, and ethical manufacturing. To strengthen sustainable sourcing, our procurement teams undergo regular training to identify and assess sustainable materials effectively. We also support handcrafted fabrics and garments using indigenous tech-niques to strengthen India’s cottage industries challenged by competition from mill-made fabrics. Lifecycle Assessment (LCA) serves as a crucial tool for assessing business and sup-ply chain sustainability. Our objective is to deliver products with improved environmental and social sustainability perfor-mance and minimal health risks. Using a cradle-to-grave LCA approach, we identify potential risks and opportunities to reduce material and resource consumption. We have internally identified Cotton, Polyster and Man-
